summary:
Simonyi's first night of operations! All tests run according to plan.

AuxTel operated smoothly until 03:28 UTC, when frequent faults forced an early shutdown.

The portable DIMM.2 was disconnected yesterday, so it was not in operation tonight.
weather_summary:
Temperatures at night ~ 9- 10 deg C, humidity ~ 17 -27 %, mild winds ~5-10 m/s.
After opening mostly clear skies, with some clouds at low elevation, cloudy in the last couple of hours.
simonyi_summary:
During the morning, the camera was set to OFFLINE for some updates by the camera team, and we found Air Compressor 2 had been off for more than a day, it was recovered. We performed hexapod warm-ups, dark image tests for camera verification, and the walkaround. During daily CalSys checkouts, the system failed when taking calsys flats, likely related to the new LED, so we skipped the daily calsys to continue with other checks.
When activating OSS, an alert appeared in the cooling system, which required resetting Chiller 1 at Level 1. A dome current issue did not allow us to slew it; after trying an exit fault and sending the dome to park position, the problem was resolved. 

We started venting around 23:30 UTC, opening the shutters and louver E1, with the EAS M1M3TS setpoints disabled for 30 minutes as required Then switched to prepare-for-on-sky configuration at 00:00 UTC. Minor camera issues reminded us that tracking must be active for any exposures. Finally, we proceeded with BLOCK-T539 initial alignment using the new hexapods configuration.

Late shift OS team finished initial alignment, we achieved thermalization today! 
The first run of the stability test showed unexpected variation increasing AOS residuals from 0.4" ti 0.75" (BLOCK-T614). The FBS LSST survey (BLOCK-T624), AOS residuals remained below 0.5, but later on transparency decreased . Last on sky test was repeating the stability test, where AOS residual remained between 0.3" to 0.4" .  We closed the dome at 7:50 UTC, DomeAz failed and we used RecoverFromControllerFault.py which worked! 
Finally we run the Daily calibrations.  

We had 2 occurrances for the mirror cover failing to closed (OBS-1154)
auxtel_summary:
AuxTel startup was normal. At the beginning of the day time checkout, we found the interlock door open, and after closing it, we start venting at 16:16 CLT, then we go to the sky at 20:45 CLT.

AuxTel run smoothly until 3:28 UTC, we had repeated Azimuth max tachometer difference exceeded (OBS-1294). We also have an issue of CSC and controller status were mismatched (OBS-1269), as transparency reported by LSSTCam was low, we decided to shutdown at 5:30 UTC.
observers_crew: Gonzalo Aravena;Carlos Morales;Paulina Venegas;Jacqueline Seron;Keith Bechtol;Erik Dennihy

summary:
We completed all scheduled Simonyi tests, though we encountered some issues during the run. We observed thermal degradation and disabled the M1M3TS setpoints in the EAS. Overall, transparency stayed at 1.2, and the median PSF FWHM ranged from 0.9″ to 1.0″. At night we run mostly AOS tests and 30 min of FBS survey.

AuxTel showed frequent faults after venting, so we decided not to operate it tonight.
weather_summary: At night: temperatures ~ 6- 8 deg C, humidity ~ 17-44%, moderate winds ~4-9 m/s. Some thin clouds, with thicker clouds at low elevation.
simonyi_summary:
During the morning, we performed hexapods warm-ups and telescope was at the horizon, so we encountered some issues during the M2 hexapod warm-up in each axis, hexapod was re enabled with configuration v20 and tested axis by axis, only axis z failed after 3 attempts. After redeploying the correct version of the LED Projector on ArgoCD, the daily CalSys checkouts were carried out successfully (ignoring electrometer 103). The dome handover took place without issues at 18:30 UTC. Then we performed Bumpt test, hardpoint break away and TMA checkouts, with no major issues. Lover E1 was opened at 22:30 UTC and shutters at 23:00 UTC. EAS was back to its normal configuration after 30min of venting. Prepare for on sky was performed to open mirror covers and then we just wait until having enough darkness to start with Initial Alignment BLOCK-T539.

Initial alignment BLOCK-T539 converged successfully to 0.4”.  We then moved to Full Array Mode closed-loop (BLOCK-T492). During this test, we had multiple MTAOS heartbeats lost,  and residual AOS increased to 0.6". So before moving to the next test, we run a close_loop reaching 0.45”. We continue with the Check Filter offset for igzr bands (BLOCK-T559).

The M1M3–dome temperature difference remained at ~0.5°C until 03:30 UTC, then rose rapidly to 1°C. At ~04:10 UTC, Brian S. adjusted the M1M3TS setpoints, improving the situation. EAS was re-enabled with M1M3 setpoints disabled. 

During the Hartmann Giant Donut Sensitivity test(BLOCK-T621), we had a MTRotator FAULT (OBS-902, 20 min lost).

During the FBS survey (BLOCK-T624), MTAOS faulted due to MTRotator not reporting angle (OBS-1304, 48 minutes lost) recovered and managed to run the scheduler for ~30 minutes. The median PSF FWHM was approximately 1.0”, AOS residuals ~0.3 - 0.4, and transparency remains ~1.2. Unfortunately, we had some sphericals due to thermal gradients. 

We closed the dome at 8:25 UTC and run daily calibrations, but were interrupted by OBS-1305. We decided to park TMA.
auxtel_summary: AuxTel checkouts started at 17:50 UTC, and venting began at 19:10 UTC, but multiple issues occurred with the ATMCS system (OBS-1294), so the telescope was left closed and Craig mentioned it could be reviewed tomorrow.
observers_crew: Gonzalo Aravena;Carlos Morales;Jacqueline Seron;Paulina Venegas;Bruno Quint;Keith Bechtol

summary:
During the daytime, we had Kafka/internet issue during the day and needed to recover several system back including M2. We had filter position swarp and installed y filter during the day as well. We had dome shutter issue was solved re-making the procedure waiting longer in each step. Lastly, there was a network outage on some network devices at the summit.

AuTel daytime works on tachometer and AT Mount were successful. Most of the observing night was peaceful for AT.

Unfortunately for Simonyi we lost almost the entire night due to a series of major faults that reduced total on sky time to about 30 - 45 minutes. At the end of the night, we saw the same network behavior again, and several CSCs of MT faulted. Luckily we were already closed, but M2 remained in open loop. Despite troubleshooting, we were unable to clear blocking interlocks and we have to leave the TMA in its current state.
weather_summary: Pretty bit cold (~ 13 C) and low humid (~ 16 %) but relatively high wind speed (8 - 11 m/s) during the day. But the wind went down to ~ 3 m/s when we opened the dome. DIMM.1 and DIMM.2 are working fine
simonyi_summary:
During the day, as planned, y and u filters installed on instrument in the loader 1 and 2 each successfully. So, the final filter-set of tonight was iygzr. We performed change filter exercise for four times between u and y and worked very well.

We had a Kafka/internet issue due to pixel firewall work from IT and most of the system (ESS, MTM2, M1M3) went to FAULT and recovered them in ~ 40 mins.

During the dome handover (started 19:38), we had dome shutter fault issue. Even with several exitFaults and resetDrives, we couldn’t open the dome shutter and went to fault in the BLOCK-T70. Gonzalo M. found there was a general fault related to motor and manually reset drives but didn’t work. Even clear the emergency stops on the panel, we couldn’t clear the issue. Even we went up to the top of the dome to check other interlocks and emergency stops, we couldn’t any special related to this until 22:30 UTC. But finally, we could finally find the issue and could complete dome handover at 23:25 UTC (~3.5 hours).

After that, the night got worse. Shortly after getting on sky, dynalene chiller 01 failed and we had to swtich, causing a 3-hour delay for camera. Then, briefly after taking images, the network crashed and we lost most AT and MT systems. We had to call for help to recover the GIS and go back on sky. Shortly after that, M1M3 faulted, and we had to do 45 minutes of recovery and health checks. We closed early and ran dynamic tests instead. We were unable to take daily calibrations because the fiber spectrograph faulted.
auxtel_summary:
In the daytime, Manual, Migual, Braulio, and Craig did AuxTel maintenance on the tachometer fails, AuxTel Az mount functionalities. After that, daytime checkout completed successfully. AuxTel venting proceeded till sunset without any faults. AuxTel on sky observation started at 23:44 UTC and finished Scheduler at 08:55 UTC.

If it hadn’t been for the network outage, perhaps it would have been a night without major issues. During the network outage, AuxTel also failed, but was able to recover.

summary:
We had a GIS and lost connection with the LOVE issue today. We lost a lot of heartbeats of CCSs and couldn't access LOVE for 2.5 hours today, so we started our daily checkouts a bit late after the dome handover. There was work in the mirror cell investigating the FCU problem during the day. There was a filter-changing waking-up test for the first time.

We also needed to manually turn off the dome lights due to a lost connection issue with Shelly (OBS-1316). Also, due to a repetitive fault, LSST_WAP was removed from the dome tonight, so we used RubinObs-Guest and connected to the base VPN. We had lost connection with LOVE for 2.5 hours during the daytime.

****
weather_summary: It was also mid-warm and mild weather during the day. Temp ~ 13 - 16 C, Wind ~ 8 m/s, and Humidity ~ 14 %. But the temperature dropped down to ~ 11 C when we opened the dome. Weather cooperated all night.
simonyi_summary:
The day started with M1M3 FAULT and was followed by MTM2 FAULT. We could see four interlocks activated in GIS, and Franco C. told us to investigate and recover systems from the GIS issue. Petr et al. worked in the mirror cell to check what the problem is with 65. FCU 66 fan didn't turn on, it seems like either a breaker issue, or cabling, or ILC. There was a problem with FCU 79, restarting CSC, and they fixed it. 

While waiting for the GIS issue and M1M3 mirror cell work, we ran the test 'wakeFilterChanger' (BLOCK-T631) from Alexandre's request. But we had MTRotator FAULT (Pull Cord issue, OBS-875), and we decided to wait for MTRotator to be ready. After this, we faced a lot of HB lost critical alarms and lost connections to LOVE at ~ 15:30 UTC. After 2.5 hours, we could finally access LOVE at ~17:49 UTC. So, we could start our daily routine with the hexapod warm-ups.

The dome handover started at 18:48 UTC and finished in 5 minutes without any issues today. While performing Bump and HP tests, we successfully ran the waking-up filter changer test (BLOCK-T631). There was another LOVE connection issue at ~ 21:10 from the observer's workstation, but we could access LOVE in 30 mins. We started BLOCK-T634 for TMA Balance check with parking speed but had M1M3 FAULT at el ~ 4 deg. 

After raising M1M3 again, we started TMA checkouts and finished the daily calsys checkout. At 23:34, we opened the dome shutter and louver. We created a ticket requesting an updated test case for 'ensure_onsky_readiness.py' to avoid repeated failures caused by the AOS closed-loop status (OBS-1318). Simonyi was on-sky at ~ 00:10.

Shortly after getting on sky, the camera team alerted us to a dynalene emergency. They had to power off all CCDs and REBs. Recovery took several hours, but we determined that getting back on sky was a risk with the camera in an unsecured state. We spent the remainder of the night doing calibration and CBP testing. (OBS-1310)
auxtel_summary: We started AuxTel daytime checkouts at 13:55 UTC and AuxTel venting from 15:20 UTC. Auxtel started on-sky observation at 23:37 UTC. AuxTel observed smoothly all night! No faults to report.

summary:
There was mirror cleaning and generator testing. And the Camera team worked on recovering the rubber cover issue and the Dynalene issue from last night. There were EAS, M1M3FC, and frequent ESS faults during the day. 
Still, the Shelly connection is not available.  The night was dedicated to AOS testing. No cals for today due an issue with the camera at the end of the operations (cals time)
weather_summary: It was a mid-warm day with a mean temperature of ~14 degrees C. The average humidity was ~ 15% and the average wind speed was around 7 m/s. When we started the night operations, the temperature dropped to ~ 11 C. For the rest of the night, the wind remained stable and low (around 5 m/s). The temperature dropped slightly to about 9 °C by the end of the night, with clear skies throughout.
simonyi_summary:
Mirror cleaning was done in the morning. camera team checked dynalene, Cyro3, and the rubber cover. They found the rubber cover is not the velcro issue, but more with the glue. So, they reattached it temporarily for this weekend but will fix it more properly next week. The electronics team also tested remote start generators.

We started the Hexapod warm-up around 13:51 UTC. Daily calsys checkout started at 16:10:57 UTC. But there was an EAS fault at 15:04 UTC, it seems like this is related to the MTmount CCW only mode. Here is the ticket for this issue (OBS-1319). M1M3TC went to fault when we parked the TMA to the horizon, and we created a ticket for this (OBS-1320). ESS 107 and 108 went to fault 5 times during the day (OBS-1323). 

The dome handover was completed at 19:00 UTC. They said the SELLY connection issue is fixed, but it's still there. When we ran the filter exercise, we found that the filter name was not matched between RubinTV and the telemetry in the chronograph (OBS-1322). But we could check the filter is right so that we could finish other checkouts. 

The dome shutter and louver were opened at 23:14 UTC. We began with the initial alignment, followed by running LUT-005. During this test, multiple CSCs failed (MTMount, MTRotator, and MTPtg), triggered by the CCW — please refer to OBS-738 for details. Approximately 20 minutes were lost. Most of the sky time was dedicated to this test.  We ran out of time for the last elevation 25.

At the end of the night, we performed the LSSTCam Whitelight Flats (single LEDs), we got a camera issue related to cryo 6 trip off, and this issue ended the night without the cals.
auxtel_summary: We started Auxtel daytime checkout at 14:45:39. Then, we started Auxtel venting at 15:08:13. The Auxtel observation started at 23:38 UTC.  It was a flawless night for AuxTel operations.
observers_crew: Minhee Hyun;Lukas Eisert;Narayan Khadka;Paulo Lago;Kshitija Kelkar

summary:
Halloween Hauntings --- Daytime operation was very smooth and Narayan could get good exercise for driving for a whole day. Kevin F. and day crew tarped DIMM.2 to prepare cold and windy weather in the weekend.

Lost majority of tonight due to humidity, and clouds -- close-dome time was dedicated to TMA dynamic tests, Whitelight flats, and CBP QE sweeps. 
We went onsky in last 1.5 hrs, challenging our systems with insufficient thermalising time, bad seeing and borderline trim heat capacity for Camera. We managed to sail through the dark veil by ending the night with initial alignment and getting focus sweep data.
weather_summary:
We could feel it was bit colder than yesterday (~ 10 C) and more humid 43 %. Also, we could see sky covered by more cirrus as time goes by as the weather forecast expected. But last 3 hours before going on sky, weather was dramatically changing and from ~ 23 UTC, humidity rise up so quickly from 60 % to 80 % in 1 hour. Generally a windy night with three celestial visitors in the sky (Commets Lemmon, Swan, Christensen)

First 3 hrs after sunset were humid (>65% relative humidity) and later half of the night was completley overcast
simonyi_summary:
We finished Hexapod warm-ups, daily calsys before Simonyi walkaround. And we recognized downdraft fan was still on, so turned it off. During the morning, Stuart and OSes did cooling down Cryo 6 temperature because it hit the limit of temperature. Kevin F. and day crew tarp DIMM.2 to prepare cold and windy weather in the weekend (confluence page for direction to tarp DIMM is created with training video).

After we finished dome handover at 19:15 UTC, we ran other checkouts including bump and HP tests. There was Home failed related EIB issue (OBS-1326). We opened dome and louver at 23:18 UTC (humidity ~ 60 %). We were all set for onsky but humidity reached eventually to 80 % so quickly, so we closed the dome immediately at 23:44 UTC. 

The dome never go reopened due to fluctuating humidity, continuous drop in ambient outside temperature (resulting in high Delta between In-dome and outside temperature) and later dense cloud coverage.

We focused on dynamic tests at 20% performance TMA settings and getting calibrations data (whitelight flats (y,z,r,i,g) & CBP QE sweeps (no filter)). Dynamic tests were a success at elevations 40 and 70 deg (detailas in #m1m3-worklog). Monochromatic  flats could not be accomplished because we faced issues powering off tunable laser required between filter change (OBS-1230). It is possibly linked to unstable dome WiFi. This caused ESS.119 to lose heartbeats as well. 
We did have random rotator fault during the CBP sweep. 

We went on sky for last 1.5 hrs before dome closing --- we had a 4C temperature difference between inside and outside to minimize, get initial alignment done with overall bad seeing and work within a window of minimal heat capacity for Camera. All went fine and we squeezed in some focus sweep data which hopefully will be useful for relative detector height characterisation and contribution to our delivered IQ.  

There was an IT issue, Minhee couldn't log-in workstation 1 (IHS-9524). Baden said this is related to the persistent crashing from CPS overload issue. So, please everyone close every sessions after the shift on Workstation 1/2.
auxtel_summary:
There was a LATISS checkout failed and ATCamera fault in the morning. Even we cleared alerts/faults in ATCamera from ccs, we couldn't proceed. It was from daq-monitor (OBS-1325). After Gregg fixed the DAQ, we could finish checkouts without any fault. 

After venting for the whole day from 17:54 UTC, we started on-sky observation at 23:40 UTC but because of high humidity (> 80%), we shutdown AuxTel immediately.
observers_crew: Minhee Hyun;Lukas Eisert;Narayan Khadka;Paulo Lago;Kshitija Kelkar

summary: Very calm day with no notable issues. We had no AOS Support so the night was filled by FBS observations and stability tests.
weather_summary: The beginning of the night was very clear, warm (8deg) and reasonably dry (35%) but had stronger winds 14m/s compared to last night. The night started with the moon close to the zenith.
simonyi_summary:
All daily tasks completed without issues.

Petr tested the auto enable balance forces after raising the mirror. It failed at el = 22 deg but succeeded at el = 45 deg. Therefore, for now we shall raise above 45 degrees. If below, move on static support with 5% max speed to  >45 deg before raising.

We started the initial alignment at 00:16 UTC and completed at 01:09:48 UTC. AOS stability verification started at 01:14 UTC and was completed at 02:21 UTC. MTAOS went into fault at 02:43 UTC, and we noticed significant image degradation. We recovered the MTAOS and reset the AOS to the last good image (sequence 103). However, MTAOS went into fault repeatedly (three times) and also repeated failures of the track target and take image scripts happened. As a result, we lost approximately three hours of observing time. Observations resumed at 05:40 UTC. The daily calibration checkout completed at 9:50 UTC.
auxtel_summary:
During Auxtel Pneumatics Checkout we encountered a fault cause by the Hexapod Offset being at -9632342  in z direction which failed the ATAOS and AT Hexapod. We solved it by restarting the ATAOS CSC. More details in OBS-1327. Other checkouts, venting and going onsky had no issues.

The Auxtel observation stated at 00:41:37 UTC. At 02:12 UTC, wind speed is ~14 m/s. We shutdown the Auxtel at 2:19 UTC.

summary: Very quiet day and an OBS-fest night with no issues. We removed the tarp from DIMM.2 and enabled it together with DIMM.1.
weather_summary:
Early night was warm (10-9 deg) and clear with slightly less wind than yesterday (<4m/s). Humidity close to 35%.
At the start of the night, the almost full moon was at zenith. 
Winds picked up later in the night (10-15m/s).
simonyi_summary:
All warmups and checkouts finished without issue.
We started to vent the dome at 23:04 UTC and started the initial alignment at 00:00 UTC. 

Smooth night with AOS verification at the start (initial alignment, effect of relative chip heights on delivered FWHM, filter offsets and AOS stability) and FBS (with injected triplet sequences) for the remainder of the night. Lots of interesting discussion FWHM across the focal-plane, PSF ellipticities etc--> follow slack threads! 

Night ended with daily calibs and i-band flat offs left running. Discussion initiated about about Lasertracker stabilising times during calibrations and how can we bring down the execution time of daily Calibs (initial setup+actual data taking; OBS-1334).
auxtel_summary:
Auxtel checkouts completed without issues. We took the weekly calibrations and vented the whole afternoon.
Auxtel went on sky at 23:43UTC.
30 min Observing time loss in between due to winds. 
End of observations at 08:00 UTC

summary:
Relatively smooth day transitioning into a smooth start of night.
Relatively smooth night operation, only one dome failure. Cloudy weather during the night, and seeing not good.
weather_summary:
Decreasing clouds throughout the day, with moderate winds.  After sunset, winds around 9m/s and humidity at 50% and rising slowly.
Humidity goes down from 50% to 20% during the night. Wind around 10-15m/s. Fast moving clouds, sky changing rapidly from fully cloudy to almost all clear.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime checkouts: hexapod warmups passed quietly, but the M1M3 bump test encountered some issues (OBS-1335).  TMA checkouts completed but MTCamera went to fault due to a jgroups meltdown for unknown reasons (OBS-1336).  All the lights on L5-L8 were left on, and dome lights cannot be switched remotely (OBS-1316).  After the recovery from the meltdown, it took several attempts to recalibrate the shutter timing due to unknown reasons.  Dome and louver were opened before sunset for venting, and the control room enjoyed several minutes of calm while waiting for the sky to get dark enough for initial alignment.  


The night operation started with block T635 camera focus sweep. We ran the block 3 times for more data, then switched to BLOCK-T559 Filter Offsets LUT.  After that, we switched to T395 camera rotator LUT. We had a dome motion state error (OBS-646), but it was recovered quickly with exitFault.  DIMM.1 stopped reporting at ~04:00UTC. We brought it back for a short while by recycling DIMM.1, then it faulted again and was recovered by Brian Stalder. Starting at ~4:10UTC we got scattered moonlight from clouds, affecting the images at EL=40. We decided to stop the block and switch to FBS with bad seeing (T630).  We set the EAS configuration to a fixed setpoint for testing at 4:30UTC.

At 7:30UTC the sky turned clear. We went back to T395 camera rotator LUT. After a few closed loop iterations, we only had time to finish EL 25 which were missing earlier due to clouds. We started block T614 AOS stability test at 8:30UTC, and we were only able to finish step 3 before closing the dome. During the daily calibration, script failed with a seemingly connection issue (OBS-1337), we are left at 30 out of 50 PTC taken. We parked TMA and left at 7AM CLT.
auxtel_summary:
AuxTel checkouts were done early and the telescope was left venting all day.  AuxTel started observing automatically and on time.
Auxtel on sky smoothly for the whole night.
observers_crew: Eric Christensen;Kate Napier;Shuang Liang;Danica Žilková;Kevin Fanning

summary: Smooth day and night for both Simonyi and Auxtel.
weather_summary:
Clear with lower winds, humidity and less clouds than yesterday. 
Throughout the night, there was relative humidity of 30 - 40% and wind speed of 10 - 12 m/s. Slightly worsened seeing, ranging between 1.1 - 2.0.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime work was relatively smooth, aside from the need to mostly power down LSSTCam during a scheduled dynalene maintenance outage.  Daily checkouts and on-sky preparation went well, and the dome was opened for venting a few minutes before sunset.

Beginning of the night we run the T635, testing camera focus sweep on dZ four times. Then proceeded with T559 checking filter offsets. During the last exercise MTRotator faulted and was recovered by cycling the MTRotator. Fault is linked to an already existing OBS-922 ticket. We ran T599 partially again after Guillem and Tiago implemented new configuration. Afterwards we proceeded with the T614 AOS stability verification running the blocks on default config and triplets of images at one position. 

Then we continued with T624 feature based scheduler for over two hours before closing the dome at 5:20 CLT. 
While running the feature based scheduler, the Scheduler 1 faulted and after enabling the scheduler it went to Standby. Issue is linked to OBS-1341. Scheduler 1 was re-enabled and we continued with T624 scheduler. 

At the end of the night we performed the calibrations without issues and ended the night at 7:00 CLT.
auxtel_summary: Another smooth startup for AuxTel: essentially automatic checkouts, venting and scheduler start. Auxtel continued with smooth night observations until 5AM CLT.
observers_crew: Eric Christensen;Kate Napier;Shuang Liang;Danica Žilková;Kevin Fanning

summary:
Power glitches caused many systems to fault during the morning. After recovery from day crew and the OSs, operations were smooth throughout the afternoon. However, TMA had interlock issues in the evening (troubleshooting lasted ~3hrs). This significantly delayed our on-sky preparations.
The night went smoothly overall, with a few minor fails that did not interrupt observations, and we were able to maintain stable operations throughout.
weather_summary: Weather peaked at ~12C during the day and dropped to ~8-9C near sunset. Wind speeds were <10m/s and the relative humidity stayed around 20-30% throughout the day. The temperature kept on decreasing throughout the night down to 4 degrees, wind remained moderate between 10 - 14 m/s. Seeing was on average around 1.5. Few cirrus clouds appeared at the beginning of the night and then dispersed.
simonyi_summary:
We started the morning with a power glitch at the observatory. It caused dynalene, TMA IS, GIS, and M2 CSC issues. We were temporarily on generator power during the recovery process, and we switched back to commercial power 13:00 UTC. The electrical team continued running the Caterpillar generator for further testing in the morning. We began normal OS operations around the same time, starting with hexapod warmups and the calibration system checkout.

By midafternoon, we completed bump and hardpoint tests. However, around 20:40 UTC we were unable to turn on the power supply for the TMA. It was discovered that there was a GIS interlock on the OSS, which Franco and Ian worked to correct. We were given control of the TMA at 23:50 UTC, completed the checkout, and prepared for venting at 00:00 UTC (sun elevation -11°). Due to this delay, we decided to skip directly to opening the dome, ignoring the 30 min of venting procedure due to the time crunch (and the outside and inside temperatures were similar).

We opened the dome with EAS in its normal configuration but moved back to m1m3ts disable after about 40 minutes, then a fault in the onsky_readiness script occurred while homing the TMA, requiring us to proceed step-by-step manually to open finally the mirror covers. Part of the night team went up to Level 8 with the IR camera to take images of the mirror-cover motors once they were fully opened. 

After that, we began initial alignment (BLOCK-T539_hexapod and BLOCK-T539), followed by three focus-sweep runs (BLOCK-T635) using the same configuration as the previous night. Around 02:25 UTC we experienced an M1M3TS failure “Cannot reset EGW pump error 59” (OBS-1344), which occurred right after a three-phase power glitch; Petr recovered the system at 02:58 UTC, and Erik restored DIMM-1 near 03:10 UTC. We continued with Filter Offsets (BLOCK-T559) and later moved to BLOCK-T614 and BLOCK-T614_triplets at azimuths −180° and −90°. As outside temperatures dropped close to 04:50 UTC, several M1M3TS over-temperature alerts led us to set the disable configuration to m1m3TS and then switch to FBS survey for the rest of the night. 

We closed the dome at 08:10 UTC and went back up to lvl 8 to take new IR images of the mirror-cover motors (posted on slack) before starting the morning calibrations.
Morning calibrations completed with no major issues...
When we started to send the TMA to horizon we got an error with m1m3 related to the active state of the mirror, at the same time we got an OSS fault, which caused OSS to turn off, we tried to reset the IS from the GIS cabinet but the credentials did not work and the account got blocked, so we were not able to reset the IS. Erik helped us to bring the system back at 10:45 UTC and then we enabled OSS to send TMA to horizon again and turned off OSS. 
Due to time constrains we were not able to extend the DPs
auxtel_summary:
Craig and Fritz spent the morning inspecting the electronics near the vent fan, as we have had incidences during the winter of snow blowing inside the dome and melting. Afterward, Mario completed a safety evaluation, and we could proceed with checkouts and venting in the midafternoon. AuxTel started on-sky preparations without any issues.

Smooth night operations with no issues, closing at 07:50 UTC
observers_crew: Carlos Morales;Kristopher Mortensen;Shuang Liang;Gonzalo Aravena;Danica Žilková

summary:
No scheduled on-sky operations for Simonyi today. OS daytime operations were delayed until the afternoon due to mirror cleaning and other day work. Weather has been very cold and cloudy, so it is a perfect day to focus on calibrations!
Smooth calibration night, no major failures/faults.
weather_summary:
Temperatures dropped significantly from the previous day, averaging around 2-3°C in the morning. Wind speeds have been >10m/s, and relative humidity is consistently high at around 60-70%.  

By the evening, the humidity jumped to 100% humidity, and clouds covered the entire sky outside of the observatory. Temperatures also dropped to -2°C, but wind speeds are <5 m/s. A little bit of snow floating in the air.

Humidity at ~80% for the whole night, started decreasing at the end of the night. Wind around 6m/s.
simonyi_summary:
Today is a closed dome day for Simonyi, so we waited until day crew completed the mirror cleaning prior to starting any daytime operations with the MTCS components. Day crew also inspected the oil tray for any leaks/blockages due to a noticeable raise in the oil level yesterday. The electrical also spent half of the day working on the UPS in the server room, and they worked on the Mistubishi generator afterward.  We completed the daily calsys checkout and bump tests.

By around 17:30 UTC, we were able to start with hexapod warmups and bump tests. Air Compressor 2 powered off unexpectedly (OBS-1215), but we quickly recovered by resetting it and powering it back on with a run_command. Dome handover was shortened since we will not open the shutters today. Prior to starting TMA checkout (22:00 UTC), we noticed multiple incidences of M1M3TS faulting from an error with the EGW pump, and required Petr to restart the CSC (logged in OBS-1344 due to similar issues).

We completed hardpoint breakaway test and TMA checkout, and then proceeded with in dome testing at 23:30 UTC, starting with the CBP no filter sweep test.

The night shift started with debugging CBP laser. We started taking QE sweep data at ~00:40AM UTC, which finished at 01:50AM UTC. We then switched to T523 Monochromatic flats. We met an issue with add_block id:BLOCK-T523_6, where we cannot power off the tunable laser (OBS-1230). We continued with turning on and off the laser manually with run_command. The script take_calsys_flats_lsstcam.py wasn't accessible in MTQ, and Elana loaded it with run_command -- showSchema.

After the 2 hours of non-filter flat sweep, Parker fixed the scripts for powering on and off the tunable laser, so we continued the Monochromatic flats with filters via add_block. We realized the none filter flat-offs after wavelength scan was missing, and we made them after taking y-band data. We then followed the order of z, i, r, g bands for the Monochromatic flats. We finished the block at 9:30AM UTC and ended the night.
auxtel_summary:
Checkouts were delayed to midafternoon due to day work. Craig spent the morning running mount tests, and Mario completed the mirror cleaning until in the early afternoon. Around 8:26 UTC we were able run the daytime checkouts, but bad weather prevented us from starting venting or on-sky procedures.
Weather didn't improve over the night. We shut down Auxtel at 6:30AM UTC.
observers_crew: Kristopher Mortensen;Carlos Morales;Shuang Liang;Gonzalo Aravena;Danica Žilková;Elana Urbach;Marina Pavlovic

summary:
We had an M1M3TS issue with the safety signal for glycol leak (OBS-1344), and it is still not fully resolved. We made a test case for louver checking in the dome handover and it finished successfully. Workstation 1 suddenly reboots itself (OBS-1308, OBS-1339) twice today. We had M1M3TS-related FAULTS just before sunset, and OSS also went into fault. A lot of difficulties just before Onsky. But we could take IR images before Onsky.
Night time operations was good overall, minor issues encountered
weather_summary:
Still bit cold. Daytime temp was ~ 5 C to 9 C. Low humidity ~ 14 to 34 %, and mid wind speed ~ 6 to 4 m/s.
Overnight temps decreased slowly to 6.5°C and humidity remained relatively stable around 32%. Windspeed around 9 m/s
simonyi_summary:
We checked the cleaning of the glycol filter for Dynalene, which was finished yesterday. There was an M1M3 and an M1M3TS FAULT in the morning. Especially, the M1M3TS fault (OBS-1344) was related to the safety signal of glycol leak, triggering the pump stop. Franco, Robinson, and Petr (remote) worked to identify and fix the M1M3TS glycol pump problem inside the mirror cell from ~ 17 UTC. The issue was from lost communication between the flow meter and the VFD pump. After they had been working on that issue for about two hours, both the pump and the flow meter were back. They assumed the communication issue is in the connectors and they will dig into this more on Monday. After working on them, we did the Bump and HP test, and nothing special. But at 19:38 UTC, the thermal system failed again with error 59, safety signal. So, the summit crew needs to keep an eye on the M1M3TS issue during the weekend. Petr gave us instructions on that fault. 

The dome handover was finished around 18:55 UTC. During the dome handover, we tested the Louvers too by opening 10% of them, especially since the electronics team wanted to test them. Workstation 1 had a sudden shutdown issue (OBS-1308, OBS-1339). We finished the other checkouts without any problems. But, at 22:38 UTC, we got M1M3, M1M3TS, and MTMount Fault while just waiting for sunset. This was also related to the M1M3TS issue, which started with the thermal interlock. While recovering from this event, we encountered an OSS fault at ~23:01 UTC (OBS-1352), opened the MTDome opened in the meantime, OSS took 45 minutes to power back on, we were just in time and we started initial alignment ~ 21:25 UTC. 

After completing the initial alignment, we proceeded with the Stability Verification (BLOCK-T614). during the second pointing we had MTRotator FAULT due to delayed telemetry from CCW (OBS-992), we then run the remaining iterations to finish it. Also we had an EAS fault (OBS-1353), re-enabled with default configuration. 
When the OSS fault occurred, we noticed that the TMA Thermal System had turned off and was no longer tracking ambient conditions on the azimuth drives, elevation drives, and Cabinet 0101, with no specific alert for this situation. 
After finishing the stability verification, we re-enabled ambient tracking for the drives and Cabinet 0101. We then moved to BLOCK-T635 (Focus Sweep), but due to not optimal image quality, we repeated the initial alignment and after that, we continued with BLOCK-T559 (Filter Offsets), where the OBS-922 issue appeared again. 
After running the filter offsets successfully, we performed another alignment before transitioning to the FBS survey. During scheduler operations, the MTPtg failed due to a rotator motion lock; after recovery, we noticed that the scheduler had sent a disable command to the AOS closed loop without re-enabling it, so we paused the scheduler to correct this and proceeded. We finished the scheduler run at 08:10 UTC, closed the mirror covers and dome, though the mirror covers’ X+ side failed (OBS-979), and then we completed the night with calibration sequences. We got two faults taking calsys flats (OBS-1355). Due to time constrains we decided to finish Simonyi operations.
auxtel_summary:
Daytime checkouts and venting were very smooth. On-sky observation started 21:45. 
Flawless night for AuxTel, closing at ~08:20 UTC
observers_crew: Carlos Morales;Minhee Hyun;Gonzalo Aravena;Jacqueline Seron;John Franklin Crenshaw;Marina Pavlovic

summary:
Quite smooth day, only TMA pointing issues in the BLOCK-T436_v5 but fixed. There was M1M3 thermal gradient issue. 
Challenging FBS night with Simonyi, persistent mount and tracking faults along with encoder, but in general only a bit more than an hour was lost. At the end of the night OSS failed and calibrations also had issues.
weather_summary:
During the day, the temperature dropped from 14 to 9 degrees Celsius. Humidity began to rise from 25% to 32%.
Wind speed has remained constant between 6 and 7 m/s.
The wind direction was erratic until 22:00 UTC, then stabilized at 0 degrees.
DIMM.1 and DIMM.1 in Enabled mode.
During the night, temperatures dropped from 7.7 to 5.5°C, Humidity reached 66% around 08:00 UTC and windspeed between 7 and 8.5 m/s
simonyi_summary:
A quiet day at the observatory. The warm-up and daily calsys checkouts were completed without incident. The telescope walk-around was also performed without problems. Around midday, work began on BLOCK-T436 (v5). Some measurements were taken, but the block needed repair due to TMA pointing issues (OBS-1356). Tiago fixed the problem, but verification was not possible due to time constraints.

During the afternoon, the mirror exhibited a temperature gradient of 1 degree. Petr suggested sending the TMA to the horizontal position to release heat, which was done. Unfortunately, the MTM1M3 failed, and everything, including the mirror's thermal system, had to be recovered. We continued cooling at an elevation of 75 degrees.

When running the TMA checkout, a problem was detected with the filter system OBS-910, 

The night began smoothly with initial alignment and FBS survey scheduler under good seeing conditions (~0.8″), but later multiple faults affected operations (sad panda). The MTMount, MTPtg, and MTRotator repeatedly entered FAULT states due to locked motion errors and issues with azimuth encoder heads, requiring power cycles and unlock commands for MTMount and MTRotator (OBS-714; OBS-1079). Because of these issues we had an overall time loss over 1 hour. We also took some requested IR pictures of the Camera, M2 and Mirror cover motors at 05:30 UTC (posted on Slack). Near the end of the night, OSS failed (OBS-1267, 1 h lost) and humidity reached 66%, so we decided to stop FBS survey and close the dome shutters and louvers for proceeding to take daily calibrations, again we had a fault during daily_flat (OBS-1355), which we tried to run 3 times without success.
auxtel_summary:
We took daily calibrations. Smooth operations without any issue. AuxTel started on-sky observation at 23:48 UTC.
During the night, in two ocasions both ATMCS and ATPtg went to FAULT due to azimuth tachometer issue (OBS-1294) while tracking. Due to rising humidity exceeding 65%, we decided to shut down AuxTel operations and call the night a bit earlier 8:05 UTC.
observers_crew: Carlos Morales;Minhee Hyun;Gonzalo Aravena;Jacqueline Seron;Marina Pavlovic

summary:
Day shift with several issues. We found viscous fluid leaking on the TMA (OBS-1359). The EIB required a reboot (OBS-992), and a TMA homing problem was fixed by enabling MTDome and MTDomeTrajectory (OBS-1361). The Block-T436 LUT was completed, and a filter-change issue was resolved by restarting the OCS-bridge. ATPtg and ATMCS frequent fault (OBS-568). Venting Simonyi was delayed due to high external temperatures.

Night operations run smootly for Simonyi, good image quality and one fault that took no time fix. 
AuxTel was the opposite, several faults lead us to close earlier
weather_summary:
Clear skies, with 10 degC of outside temperature and wind of 8m/s at the opening time.

While the dome was opened we still have clear skies
Temperature varied from 9.5 to 8.0C. 
Winds between 5 - 9 m/s
Humidity was between 16% and 28 %
simonyi_summary:
It was a day shift with several issues, including two significant problems that are still under investigation.

The day started with the warm-up of both hexapods (camera and M2). After that, the dome and the TMA were checked out. During this procedure, we found two spots of viscous fluid leaking. Please see OBS-1359 for details.

During the TMA driver turning on, we had an issue with the EIB. Please see OBS-992 for details. The problem was resolved after an EIB reboot—thank you, Franco, for your support. It took 2.5 hours to fix this. Shortly after, we encountered another TMA-related issue: it was not possible to home using the script, only via the EUI. Please see OBS-1361 for details. This was a bug that was fixed by setting the MTDome and MTDomeTrajectory CSCs to Enabled.

Most of the day was dedicated to the Block-T436 LUT with the laser tracker. We completed the task, pausing briefly to troubleshoot the filter-change issue (see OBS-1361 and OBS-1079). Restarting OCS-bridge solved the filter change problem.

During the day, we could see M1M3 thermal gradients (in fact, worse than yesterday in the morning). Petr updated the set point and sped up the fan; eventually, the gradient somehow loosened.

It was not possible to vent Simonyi as desired. Based on Sun elevation and high external temperatures, the conditions only became favorable at 23:50 UTC. 

Smooth night, after initial alignment we measured PSF FWHM 0.8” and AOS residual of 0.37. 
M1M3 thermal gradients were within/closed to operational limits since the  observations started.

We run AOS tests : Camera dz Focus Sweep (BLOCK-T635), Check filter offsets (BLOCK-T559) and AOS stability verification test (BLOCK-T614). Then we run the FBS survey (BLOCK-T624) for about 3 hours, in this period Scheduler:1 went to STANDBY state by itself without warning (OBS-1362, ~5 min lost).

Dome was closed at 8:10 UTC, and we run the daily calibrations (BLOCK-T399) which completed successfully!.

We parked at zenith as Petr requested.
auxtel_summary:
One important issue occurred on AuxTel: ATMCS and ATPtg faulted during venting without an obvious cause. See OBS-568 for details. It is important to highlight that the CSC was not publishing the errorCode.

Eventful night operations:
- ATMCS FAULT (OBS-1294, ~15min lost), recovered and resumed the scheduler.
- The scheduler was sending targets below El 30, and we could not open the dropout shutter as winds were above 8m/s, we manually eliminate those scripts and continue. 
- correct pointing failed, and we spent some time solving that as te hexapod correction was disabled, then it was a timeout waiting for the TCS. 
- ATMCS persistent  FAULTs  did not allow us to move AuxTel (OBS-1294, ~2h) forcing us to close earlier.
observers_crew: Minhee Hyun;Paulo Lago;Jacqueline Seron;Lukas Eisert;Marina Pavlovic;Josh Meyers

summary:
Recovery actuators done. M1M3 and M1M3TS fault several times during the day. No filter exchange fault issue today after optimizing filter exchanger. Dome ****


No Auxtel tonight due to ATMCS and ATPtg issue (OBS-1294). 

Smooth night with Simonyi until we encountered an OSS issue, after which seeing was variable. During the night we ran 2 AOS tests and ~30 min of FBS.

DIMM.1 and DIMM.2 operated during the night, both had issues when disabling them (OBS-1365).

We had another event of Linux Workstation rebooting by itself (OBS-1308)
weather_summary:
Mild but little bit windy day. Temperature 14 to 10 C, humidity ~ 34 %, wind speed from 5 to 9 m/s during the day. DIMM.2 went to fault in daytime, we could put STANDBY but failed to put DISABLED (OBS-1363).

While the dome was opened we still have clear skies
Temperature varied from 9.5 to 6C. 
Moderate winds between 6 - 11 m/s
Humidity was between 16% and 46 %
simonyi_summary:
There was an work inside the M1M3 cell during the day by Ian, Juan, and Petr. They fixed FCU 31 and checking cabling and heater of other FCUs. Thanks for their efforts, we could use all FCUs for tonight. At 18 UTC, working in the mirror cell was done and we started bump test. But we faced several M1M3 and M1M3TS faults right after starting the test or entering engineering mode. After several recovery trials, we could finish tests and raise M1M3. 

There was an issue when we did dome handover. The internet connection with the VPN (needed to command the dome) was misbehaving, which delayed the procedure by 10 min. Also (not related to internet issue), we needed to home the dome during the process, Thank you Lorenzo for the support

There were filter changer optimization updates during the day. There was no fault during the filter checkouts. 

We opened the louvers and dome before the sunset (el = 4.2) at 22:49 UTC (19:49 CLT) based on the previous discussion with Brian. So, we could earn more venting time for better AOS alignment.

Seeing conditions were not as good as yesterday.  DIMM.1 measured seeing between 0.7″ and 1.5″, consistent with LSSTCam values. M1M3 thermal gradients stayed within or near operational limits.

We performed AOS tests: Filter Offsets Check (BLOCK-T559), then and AOS Stability Verification (BLOCK-T614), during the second TMA pointing, we had an OSS fault (OBS-1364), which caused a 2.5-hour downtime. Robinson recovered the system. We attempted another TMA second pointing, but seeing worsened, so we stopped the test.
After realigning, we briefly switched to the FBS survey (BLOCK-T624) as seeing improved to 1.1″–1.3″. 

We closed the dome at 08:10 UTC, around this time we had a MTRotator fault due to delayed telemetry (OBS-922). We completed daily calibrations (BLOCK-T399), and finally ran the M1M3 FA333 test (BLOCK-T639) which took the TMA to the parking position at horizon.
auxtel_summary: Today, again, we had very frequent ATMCS and ATPtg fault during venting (OBS-568) related to OBS-1294. Even we recovered, the issue was even more frequent as time goes by. Tomorrow, there will be azimuth drive tension adjustment. No operation tonight.

summary:
Smooth y→u filter swap and daily checkouts completed. Multiple M1M3TS/M1M3 faults occurred, TS ESSs were recovered a couple of times.
Bump tests were repeated, and filter-system tests at zenith replaced today’s filter-exchange block.
Night started with issues preventing us from aligning Simonyi. After 2,5h we were finally able to start with AOS tests.
AT had issues and was closed early.
weather_summary: Clear skies with low/no wind at the beginning of the night, humidity of 23%, Temperature around 9deg. Good sub-arcsec seeing according to both DIMMs with down to 0.75 arcsec. Humidity and Temperature rather stable throughout the night.
simonyi_summary:
We started the day with a smooth filter swap from y to u, followed by the daily checkouts and tests.
We experienced multiple issues with M1M3TS and M1M3. Several of these faults were likely caused by the thermal equipment interlock off. Thank you to Franco and Petr for the support. The M1M3 cell door interlock will be checked tomorrow; for now, it remains bypassed. The TS-related ESSs also had to be recovered a couple of times.

Due to an M1M3 fault during the bump test, the test was repeated. The hardpoints test was also performed, given the faults observed since yesterday.

Pierre Antilogus conducted several tests of the filter system with the telescope at zenith to ensure proper performance for tonight. These tests replace today’s filter-exchange block.

We started the initial alignment at 0:13 UTC and had a rough start into the night. While aligning the Telescope, we stopped receiving Data from Rapid Analysis and AOS was therefore not able to perform corrections. The first issue was related to .nan in the FITS Seeing Header which was solved as soon as the DIMM published measurements (OBS-1366). However, during the second closed loop we had a similar issue but this time it seemed to be not caused by the header but by an insufficient Quota. (Details will be added iin OBS-1367). IT (Ivan, Christian, Diego) solved it by increasing the Quota. 
At 3:30 UTC we were finally able to start with the AOS tests (Timeloss of 2-2.5h).
The rest of the night went flawless, we ran Filter Offset Checks T559, Stability Tests T614 and a bit more than 1h of FBS T624. End of night was concluded with Daily Calibrations.
TMA is at Zenith and ready for Mirrorcell Access.
At the end of the night we had some Faults of MTM1M3TS. Petr is on it.
auxtel_summary:
Craig and Manuel worked on AuxTel during the morning solving frequent ATMCS and ATPtg FAULT from previous days, and the telescope was delivered to us in the afternoon with flawless performance. There were no issues during daytime. It was reported by Frits that the remote (and local) operation of auxtel vent gate and fan is restored, but we are not operating yet.

During the night we had issues with correct_pointing failing regardless of the position. At the beginning of the night we were able to simply resume the queue but at 03:13 UTC the ACQ failed and could be not fixed because of the not working correct_pointing. Because of that we closed AT at 04:38 UTC. Details in OBS-1366.

summary:
Day started with M1M3 cell work; FCU maintenance done but FCU 80 not fixed, and Thermal System checked.
Hardpoint tests were skipped, bump tests normal; special telescope motion test performed.
Three louvers (E1, H1, H2) available tonight; quick recovery from a filter carousel fault. Mostly smooth night of observing, although while attempting to take calibrations with Simonyi, M2hexapod faults blocked that task.
weather_summary: Clear skies, low/no wind at the at the end of the afternoon, humidity around 38%. Warm end of afternoon, Simonyi dome open for vent at 22:51 UTC (before sunset).
simonyi_summary:
We started the day with the telescope at zenith and the day crew working inside the M1M3 cell. They performed maintenance on the FCUs; however, it was not possible to fix FCU 80. Petr also worked on the Thermal System. No faults were reported for either subsystem after the work was completed.

The Hardpoint tests were skipped today, but the bump tests were performed normally.
There was a special request from Petr: we moved the telescope from an elevation of 80° down to 20° using 10% performance, and later from 20° to the horizon (5 %, parking settings on), checking both the Primary and Secondary FEs. The peak value observed was 13N (force).

For tonight, we have three louvers available (E1, H1, and H2). This was arranged late in the afternoon.
By the end of the afternoon, we encountered a camera fault during the filter exercise (Carousel following error/overcurrent). The issue was quickly troubleshooted — thank you to K. Fanning for the prompt support.
The OCS-Bridge was restarted today.

AOS testing run all night, and TMA was a total peach. However, upon closing, we had issues with M2Hexapod and with M1M3. These errors blocked us from taking the cals requested, and an M1M3 fault and cascading events (OBS-1375) delayed shutting down for the night to get into optics-cleaning position. Electronics and mirror support helped us complete that task in the morning. Thanks fellas!
auxtel_summary: Today, we performed troubleshooting related to the pointing error reported on previous nights. Please see OBS-1371 for details. Thanks to Erik Dennihy and Amanda Ibsen for their support. AuxTel observations were delayed due to some suspected faulted in a push to summit_utils (OBS-1374), but we observed most of the night without incident. Some time was lost due to vignetting of the drop-out door, but no further technical faults were encountered.

summary: Several software updates were completed throughout the day. From now on, we have 4 louvers. The CO2 mirror cleaning for Simonyi and AuxTel was done. Overall a smooth night.
weather_summary: Warm day. Air temperature reached 17°C in the afternoon. Outside air temperature never went below M1M3 air temperature. So, dome shutter was opened when the Sun was at -4degree elevation. Wind speed before going into the sky was about 4 m/s, and a steady relative humidity was around 10%.
simonyi_summary:
Early morning, Sebastian A. had been updating LOVE, the current version is V6.9.3. Simonyi's mirrors were being cleaned with CO2. The M1M3 TS was restarted by Petr and Amanda from La Serena to pick up air nozzle changes. Wouter V.R. updated the MTDome CSC config to include louver E2. In total 4 louvers are available: E1, E2, H1, H2.  H1, H2 and E2 are at full performance, E1 is still in degraded performance. Te-Wei changed M2 hexapod parameters to STRUT_MAX_VELOCITY: 100 / STRUT_MAX_ACCELERATION: 100. This is due to M2 hexapod fault that happened in a short time period. Pierre was investigating what happened last night with the carousel, the controller failed before the movement. Finally, Pierre decided to roll back to the previous control software to ensure the carousel would work tonight.

Quiet calm night of AOS testing. No faults.
auxtel_summary: AuxTel behaved very well during the day, no issues to report. Mirror was cleaning with CO2 around 14:30h ChT and the Scheduler started observation when the Sun was -8 degrees elevation. We had some trouble acquiring low elevation targets, (OBS-1376), but we skipped those and continued on with little time loss.

summary: Very good day in terms of faults. No unexpected fault! ToO observation at the beginning of the night. We got some good data and alerts in the ToO program. Congrats to y'all for all the hard work that went into that!! Overall the night was smooth except for a brief dome error and an AOS closed_loops mis-configuration. AuxTel was also mostly well-behaved.
weather_summary:
A Summer warm day, temperatures reaching nearly 18°C during the afternoon. The relative humidity was below 20% during the afternoon, but before opening the dome shutter, it had increased to around 30%. Wind speed was low, approximately 6 m/s, during the evening.
At the time of opening the dome shutter, the outside temperature was 12.3°C, and the air temperature of M1M3 was 12.6°C. Mild winds and photometric conditions all night long.
simonyi_summary:
The FCS people, Pierre and Antoin, were testing/improving the carousel position precision. M1M3 thermal system CSC upgraded to properly reset error 59, meaning to avoid "not resetting EGW pump when it shall be reset". M1M3 verification, Bump test and Hardpoints Breakaway skipped, because M1M3 didn't fault last night. We continue operation with 4 louvers. All three schedulers were restarted from the ArgoCD to initialize new configuration.

Simonyi took 3 hours of ToO data! We had some trouble getting all of the desired AO testing done for not having disabled the loops after taking survey data, but we filed a ticket to improve this error reporting and moved on. We experienced a brief dome error, but we continued the rest of the night smoothly. While taking calibrations, M1M3 faulted. Luckily, only a few images were affected, and we recovered the mirror and left the telescope in calibration position.
auxtel_summary: During the daytime, AuxTel checkout and venting have been completed without issues. Observations started on time. There were some repeats of centroid script failures, but we continued passed these targets and corrected pointing when needed.

summary: A quiet but busy day. Daytime activities were devoted to dark dome tests, resolving ATPtg and ATMCS communication issues and checking in on the birdcam:).  AOS tests comprised the majority of the night, but we also got a few more ToO observations to add to  the ones collected on Friday night.
weather_summary: Minimal winds and humidity, and a generally warm day. Start of dark time was ~10C and the temperature dropped to ~8C.
simonyi_summary: The day started with M1M3 discovered in fault since after the previous shift ended. The fault was due to the M1M3 cell door open interlock activated. This repeated once more in the day before the electrical team bypassed it. The dark dome tests were conducted with TMA at horizon, and TMA and sub-system checkouts were done after that. We had a script failure while running `home_both_axes.py` (OBS-1382); unsure about the cause. Dome started venting from about 21:20 UTC, and we went on sky at 00:25 UTC.  After the initial telescope alignment, we ran BLOCK-T624 Feature Based Scheduler LSST Survey to get the remaining ToO observations from last night.  Then, since the seeing was poor ~1.6", we ran BLOCK-T641 Closed Loop Stability.  After that, we ran BLOCK-T640 Kick the Robot.  The seeing continued to improve, so we ran BLOCK-T559 Check Filter Offsets for the u- and z-bands.  We finished on-sky observations with BLOCK-T614 AOS Stability Verification - Open Loop.  After closing the dome and louvers, we ran the daily calibrations.
auxtel_summary: AT daily checkouts went fine. However, during calibration setup we had frequent ATPtg faults -- we tried 4 restarts of ATPtg, but in the end it was recovered by rebooting the cRio. Weekend calibs were started and soon aborted due to ATDome offset. AT went on sky at 9PM CLT.  There were a few occurrences of the script failing because the "centroid finding algorithm was unsuccessful" (OBS-559).  Only once did it require us to rerun the correct pointing and alignment.

summary: Dynamic tests and CBP-TMA co-pointing tests occupied the day while the nighttime was devoted to FBS (ToO) and an AOS test in between.  Smooth nighttime operations with no Simonyi or AuxTel faults except for minor dome issues.
weather_summary: Minimal winds and humidity and 11C at sunset.  Temperature oscillated between ~10.5-12C throughout the night.
simonyi_summary:
We started the day with dynamic tests -- Az & El braking tests, and opening M2 loop at STO triggers while at 20% TMA performance. All these tests were successful; we used the TMA trapped key to trigger STO. Next Fritz M. did a couple hours of CBP-TMA co-pointing tests.  We still need work on getting the dome in position for this (to be continued next weekend). 

We opened the MTDome for venting at 22:34 UTC.  After the initial telescope alignment, we ran the FBS to pick up more ToO observations in g- and i-band for the gravitational wave alert received on Friday.  Note that for exposures 34-71, there is some vignetting because we lost the dome following.  After all the ToO observations completed, we ran BLOCK-T559 Check Filter Offsets in both i- and g-band.  We finished the night by running the FBS again.
auxtel_summary: All good with AT. Weekend calibs taken today.

summary: We were able to go on-sky with both telescopes at -5 deg sun elevation. FES left the ocs-bridge in a weird state, dalmatian pattern was present in images throughout the night, WeatherForecast CSC went to fault a few times, AllSky camera has background measurements issues.
weather_summary: Warm day (around 14C) and mid-layer clouds since the afternoon. Humidity around 30%. FWHM between 0.8 and 1.4 arcsec stable all night.
simonyi_summary:
Daily checkouts went through without major issues. We had a couple of coupled TMA + M1M3 faults (one related to OSS, another one related with TMA Soft Axis Motion). Te-Wei T. performed M2Hex tests, increasing the strut acceleration and velocity for M2 Hex controller. We also had one instance of TMA faulting while restarting (Encoder fault) after applying the setting sets (OBS-965). After venting, we performed a quick rapid analysis test and then the initial telescope alignment.  We completed the ToO observations for the same gravitational wave candidate that has been observed the past few nights.  The majority of the night was dedicated to AOS tests.  We ran the daily calibrations at the end of the night. 

We got an MTDome error for azimuth, but it was solved very fast. The FES error was harder to solve because the permissions are not in place for the OS team (45 min lost).
auxtel_summary: We had a dome problem during the checkouts (OBS-1387). After it was solved, the telescope was in good shape to go on-sky. Smooth night with Auxtel just one minor issue with centroid finding algorithm was unsuccessful due to star off detector (OBS-559)

summary: Summit OS updates were done during the day. Daily checks proceed and we were done at around 19:20 CLT.  On-sky observations with Simonyi were delayed by ~2 hours due to a problem with the cryo 6.
weather_summary: Warm day with outside temperatures around 15C. Humidity around 45% but decreasing towards the end of the day. Low wind speed (<2m/s).
simonyi_summary:
Daily activities were focused on summit OS upgrades, system recovery after the upgrade and usual checkouts. We had a couple of M1M3 mirror faults related with FA 305 (OBS-1392, OBS-1393). MTCamera faced a jgroups storm that was caused by duplicate instances of the DAQ relay service for guider data running. After the OS upgrade ESS:112 and ESS:113 reported unreliable in-dome temperatures (OBS-1394), we relied on SonicTemperature for tracing the in-dome air temperature.

Cryo 6 failed at Nov 19, 0:34 UTC due to a PLC communication loss (confirmed by CCS alerts and GUI showing “PLC dead”). Despite compressor shutdown, discharge temp spiked to 122°C (unusual), and oil level dropped to ~-36mm. No prior current/voltage spikes observed; pressure trends rose slightly but unclear if relevant. PLC auto-recovered at ~1:08, and Cryo 6 was back online by 1:23. CCDs and REBs remained on, but the OSS was turned off and the dome was closed. Connectors under suspicion — follow-up planned. Root cause likely PLC Ethernet dropout; logs on pcs02 to be reviewed. (OBS-1394)

EAS had adjusted setpoint in response to faulty ESS temp readings (112-113). We changed the set points of chillers 1 and 2.  Once we were back on sky, we observed the ToO in both g- and i-bands, ran BLOCK-T559 Check Filter Offsets, and BLOCK-T645 Test the Correct Pointing Script for SimonyiTel.  At the end of the night, we ran the daily calibrations.
auxtel_summary: AuxTel daily checkout went through without issues. The first attempt at prepare for on sky froze. We shut down AuxTel and restarted the ATTCS CSC, and that solved the issue.  We ran AuxTel until 5:10 UTC since ATPtg and ATMCS CSC faulted numerous times, and several attempts to recover them were unsuccessful (OBS-568).  Since Simony had a busy day, so we just closed at 6:23 UTC.

summary: Simonyi daily checkouts were nominal. The test plan is to run smoothly.
weather_summary: Warm day with temperatures around 16C. Humidity around 30% and wind speed around 8 m/s. seeing around 1 arcsec.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime works focused on M1M3 FCU80, 23 and FA305. Daily checkout went through without issues.

We are running on Mitshubishi generator since early in the morning. The situation is going to extend until tomorrow Thursday mid-day, when the commercial power will come back. DIMM.2 suddenly faulted reporting connection issues (OBS-1398). In the afternoon, we had ingestion issues due to OODS keeping guider that would not ingest in a pending state (OBS-1399). Around 17.30 we decreased the HVAC setpoint to lower the in-dome temperature. Near sunset we test different louver settings to vent while mapping the reflections inside the dome.

The night continue without incident; the only problem was the M2 hexapod, which for some reason CSC fault when moving the TMA. (OBS-1400) The rest of the plan was The BLOCK-T645 Test the correct pointing script for SimonyiTel, Hartmann giant donut sensitivity, BLOCK-T596 LSSTCam stray light from LSSTCam autochanger and BLOCK-T399 LSSTCam Daily Calibrations.
auxtel_summary: Despite the checks done by Manuel G. during the morning, we were not able to run its checkouts nor venting in the afternoon. AuxTel is not available tonight.

summary:
Daytime main issue was related to the non-return to nominal dynalene flow, once we came back to commercial power grid. The situation forced to turn down camera system. After dynalene flow was recovered, camera was back to operations. We went on-sky around 21.00.
Disaster night, TMA debugging for 4.5 hours followed by a camera issue. No on-sky data except for initial alignment.
weather_summary:
High wind in the morning to null wind at sunset. Humidity around 40%, temperatures between 17-12C.
Quiet night, low wind, humidity ~30%.
simonyi_summary:
We had a busy day today. In the morning we had M1M3 CO2 cleaning. Nominal checkouts passed without problems. Around 15.05 we moved facility power from generator to commercial grid (passing on UPS for a few minutes). We experimented a glitch of about 30 seconds that affected mainly the dynalene system flow, it went from normal to degraded mode until it got no flux at all. It took time to recover it physically and a complete power cycle was required (FRACAS-321). The situation forced to turn down camera system. After dynalene flow was recovered, camera was back to operations at about 18.30 local.  

ESS.107 was affected and is still in the process of recovering by the time of writing (OBS-1109).

The night shift started with two MTMount faults. After recovering it, we met a time-out error in initial alignment, which turns out to be a residual issue from the power glitch earlier (wavefront sensor HV was off). After Yousuke fixed it, we went on sky shortly. We finished initial alignment and correct pointing at 01:25AM UTC. At the beginning of ToO, we met TMA fault again, which we couldn't recover. Ian E.O., David J. and Tiago helped to debug with different approaches, including restart PXI, Ethercat, and controller, then restart csc in argoCD and the TMA EUI. TMA finally brought back at 06:10AM UTC (time loss 4.5h). We focused the telescope again and started the filter offset test T559, but the camera focal plane got stuck at ACTIVE command state. We called Yousuke to fix the problem, but by the time of resolution, it is too late for any on-sky blocks. We decided to close dome ~20m early and at least the daily calibration works!.
auxtel_summary:
Mario R. and Braulio C. worked during the day to recover azimuth drive functionally. Daily checkouts passed and venting did not failed.
Auxtel on sky smoothly the whole night.

summary:
Daytime procedures were testing dynalene system and large TMA movements in response to the issues that occurred yesterday. Venting was delayed due to higher temperatures than expected. 
We could do ToO observation during the first half of nights (~ 3 hours) in the middle of TMA drives, OSS fault, and MTCamera focal plane issues. We finished BLOCK-T513, T614 (partially) and daily calibrations till the end of the night.
weather_summary: Temperatures were around 14-16°C throughout the day with low winds and low humidity. Cloud coverage was minimal in the morning but increased as the day progressed. Conditions are good for observing, but may continue to be cloudy during the night.
simonyi_summary:
In the morning, David Jimenez switched the dynalene from chiller 2 to chiller 1 as additional tests for what happened during the power change yesterday (see FRACAS-321). Overall, the camera was in safe conditions during the switch. Morning checkouts and warmups went well, and we had an early TMA handover to test azimuth/elevations drives during long slews. These tests were in response to the 4.5 hours lost last night from MTMount faults (summary and follow-up in OBS-1401). We did long slews in elevation and azimuth, and the TMA overall did well in CSC control. During dome handover, there was a request to quickly check the EGW pump on M1M3 before the day crew left for the day. As we were moving to zenith, we did not react fast enough to deploy the mirror cover while the dome shutter was being tested, resulting in a ~1min instance where the mirror was exposed in a partially opened dome. Once confirmed that the mirror was safe, we did M1M3 tests and prepared the TMA for venting. During venting, MTRotator control disable CSC commands, so we had to recover via the EUI to re-enable the CSC (OBS-1402). We then proceeded to venting, which was delayed due to higher outside temperatures than expected, and prepared for on-sky.

We opened the dome at sun elevation -9 deg (over the guide elevation for opening, -6 deg) at 00:00 UTC and started initial alignment at 00:27 UTC. After that, we performed ToO observation via FBS, BLOCK-T624 from 01:12 UTC. There were same TMA Drives issue (OBS-1401) and OSS fault (OBS-1267) at the same time at 02:17 UTC. Recovery took 25 minutes and then we could resume the ToO at 02:48 UTC again. After 04:00 UTC, the airmass of ToO reached to > 1.6 and there were camera focal-plane issue at 04:02 UTC (LSSTCAM-148, time loss ~ 20 mins).

From 04:27 UTC, we ran pointing model verification (BLOCK-T513) for 2.75 hours. At 07:28 UTC, we started BLOCK-T614, AOS stability verification - open loop, for our last test tonight. But we couldn't finished the last step of the block because of the sun elevation, and closed the dome at 08:01 UTC. Daily calibrations obtained as usual.
auxtel_summary: After a short 10min test by Mario and Juan, we ran daily checkouts and vented by midday. AuxTel continued with on-sky preparations and was observing at the start of the night (00:01 UTC). Closing AuxTel at 08:02 UTC.

summary:
Daytime testing went smoothly. All prep work was completed in time for night obs.
Troublesome night, camera faulted three times (jgroup storm), 1h time loss.
weather_summary:
Some cumulus clouds to the east, low winds, and mild to warmer temperatures.
Clear skies overnight. low winds, mild temperature and low humidity.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime work primarily focused on CBP testing, which was successful, and will continue to be optimized during the weekend. M1M3 remained raised all day. Cryo 3 was tested some more with mixed results, but we had a overall smooth day.

The night crew took over at the time of louver and shutter opening near 12AM UTC. We started initial alignment at 12:20AM UTC, then went on with ToO via FBS T624 at 1AM UTC. We met the same focal plane issue as the past few days (LSSTCAM-148), luckily Kevin was still onsite and camera was recovered in 5m. We took a few IR images in the dome before stopping ToO at ~01:50AM UTC (out of targets). We then switched to filter offset T559, followed by AOS stability T641 starting at 03 AM UTC and FBS survey starting at ~04:50AM UTC. We met twice camera faults, first one being recovered quickly but second one took ~1 hour (OBS-1336). After the recovery, AOS got out of focus and we don't have enough time for a few iterations of close loop. So we closed the dome ~5m early for daily calibration. Workstation 02 restarted itself at the beginning of daily calibration.
auxtel_summary:
AuxTel calibrations were taken, and venting since ~14h summit time.
Smooth night for Auxtel.

summary:
**ARMAGEDDON ON THE SUMMIT TONIGHT!!!**

Daytime checks were completed and passed to begin observing on sky on time. But one power glitch event sent everything south. Almost every system went to FAULT and took altogether 6.5 hours for full recovery. Finally, we managed to start the initial alignment one hour before closing and could 25 mins FBS observations.

We made 8 tickets related to all the issues from the power glitch...
Thanks for all the great efforts for recovery tonight.
weather_summary:
Clear conditions overhead with cumulus towards the east. Low winds and calm conditions at the start of the night. Perfect night  conditions, clear skies, no wind, low humidity. 

DREAM camera was on STANDBY after the power glitch.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime CBP testing was continued during the day. Preparations for on sky observations went smoothly until a mirror fault interrupted the flow. Recovery was simple with support, but will merit a follow-up (SUMMIT-11629), which has been scheduled for mirror day this upcoming week. To confront some of the camera problems of late, the ocs-bridge, focal plane, and kafka-broker-service on lsstcam-mcm were re-started.

We were able to open the dome at 00:02 UTC. When we doing initial alignment, we could see in-dome lights on in the dome monitoring camera at that moment too. We immediately stop the queue to prevent HV trip off and we recognized that there was a commercial power glitch caused a commercial power outage at the summit. This event hugely effected on many (almost) systems. 

Grand summary can be traced to OBS-1412. Systems were recovered one by one with the help of supporting scientists, camera and electrical team. First OSS and PS FAULTs were recovered - resetting alarms of the OSS Chillers 1 and 2 manually on L1 and recovering OSS by David J. Many more OSS FAULTs occurred during the night, all linked to OBS-1411. 

Meanwhile, Dynalene was running on deprecated mode, recirculating to the Camera, but no cooling capacity due to power outage. After getting back the power, Dynalene cooling was back in nominal cooling stage. Glycol chiller #2 turned off, resulting in low flowrate to Dynalene Chiller 01 and not adequate cooling. In a wrap, camera was assessed as nominal and ENABLED again. More info about the Camera issues in OBS-1407. 

HVAC system FAULT also happened during the outage, UMA LOWER 03 fan turned on when the power was back on and was turned off manually - OBS-1408. 

M1M3, MTRotator, M2Hexapod FAULTs. We cleared interlocks and cycled back to ENABLED easily. Consequently ESS.114 - 117 FAULTs recovered in GUI and cycled back to ENABLED. 

CalSys CSC’s failed to bring back to ENABLED, with FiberSpectrograph.101 and 102 FAULT - linked to OBS-1314.  Elana U. recovered the FiberSpectrographs. Also ESS.107 FAULTED and was recovered later by Fritz M. at 07:15 UTC (04:15 CLT) and that was the last system recovered tonight.

Second OSS and PS FAULT, again recovering by David J. with different issue. When trying to bring recover the TMA we got another OSS faults which were recovered by clearing the interlocks. But then when trying to put MTMount to ENABLED we got El+ limit switch lock and OSS FAULT again. This had to be recovered by David J. - the power glitch hit one of the TMA PILZ so a hard reset was required to release the El+ limit. EtherCAT issue happened as well and one of the EL drives was lost. TMA AXES PXI was requested to solve the issue (OBS-1409, OBS-1411). 

After finally getting back on sky and all systems back on, we were unable to start initial alignment after the power glitch with very strange issues - unable to take any images with close-loop - otherwise taking images fine. Close-loop seems stuck, didn't do any actions. Tiago R. helped us resolve an issue. It seemed like related to Hexapods at the first time, but actually it was more related to dome following issue (But we couldn't see any error messages or trace back during close_loop or even ensure_onsky_readness). We lost almost 2 more hours on this issue. This issue linked to - OBS-1406

Finally, after 6.5 hours of troubleshooting we were able to complete the initial alignment and start the FBS observations which took ~ 30 minutes. Afterwards we did the calibrations but there was another alignment failed because of MTMount FAULT. We could finish alignment again from the az=126.4, el=22 from our previous experiment by Shuang, Carlos, and Danica, but did not work. Then we found out the executed commands were not in fact executed - louvers remained opened, perhaps also caused issues with dome movement and alignment - OBS-1413. Finally, we finished the laser alignment and took the calibration images. Taking the PTC flats script failed, with MTCamera Error code "Lost lock on controlled subsystem focal-plane" (LSSTCAM-148), sending the MTCamera to OFFLINE as discussed with Stuart- it will be recovered during the day by the Camera team. 

FINALLY turned off the OSS and ended the exciting night parking safely at the calibration screen.
auxtel_summary: AT checks went well and the beginning of night was smooth. We began observations on time. Even-though there was a power glitch issue, AuxTel was calm and kept observing the whole night. [Good boy.]

summary: During the daytime we experienced a fault with the Camera MCM, which was recovered, and some concerning faults with the MTMount. The night crew was informed and prepared for recurrence. No more armageddon tonight, no more chaos on the summit except the Chaos Monkey. Almost every system was pretty stable during the night. We performed four AOS tests and SV in the end of the night.
weather_summary: Mild and pleasant conditions, throughout the day and night. But humidity was bit higher than yesterday (~ 40%).
simonyi_summary:
The day time checks were delayed due to works on the TMA, but no problems were felt until taking control with the CSC. We experienced an EIB and OSS fault while homing the axes and tracking an in-dome target. We are tracking this issue during the night. The OCS-bridge and kafka were restarted, and when we encountered an MCM-error when taking the first camera image. Camera support quickly helped recover, so there was not a ticket filed here.

When we did handover the operation from day crew to night crew, there was another IT related event, 'cannot login into workstation (IHS-9524). We updated temporary guideline to troubleshoot this issue. 

It was much more smooth night compared to the last night. 
We opened the louvers/dome at 23:48 UTC and started the initial alignment at 00:23 UTC. We started 'Chaos Monkey' test from 01:41 UTC to 03:15 UTC. During the test, we had some events, two MTAOS fault and MTPtg, MTRotator fault (but they recovered by recyling). Because Chaos Monkey images went to so bad and we had enough data for about 1.5 hours, we move to Filter Offset test for u and z band (BLOCK-T641) at 03:50 UTC. From 05:11 UTC, we ran Closed Loop Stability test (BLOCK-T641) at el=40 and i band, and Camera dz Focus Sweep (BLOCK-T635) 06:50 UTC. 

From 07:22 UTC, we ran FBS and calibrations till the end of the night and shutdown the Simonyi at 09:22 UTC. We park the TMA to horizon with 'none' filter for filter swap. 

DREAM was in STANDBY during the night, because circuit breaker needs to be flipped back in space (from the power glitch last night).
auxtel_summary: AuxTel passed all day time checks with flying colors and vented many hours before going on sky. Observations began on time (00:02 UTC). AuxTel shutdown at 08:00 UTC.
