summary: Daytime was smooth overall, the filter swap and TMA checkouts went well, some issues with dynalene before going onsky.  Night work was productive, completing all planned tests, despite numerous faults.
weather_summary: Clear skies with no clouds. Windspeed below 6m/s and decreasing towards the sunset, but picked up to around 10m/s through the night. Humidity dropped from 45% to 12% by night's end.  Seeing around 1.5" at start of the night, improving to sub-arcsecond for the second half of the night.
simonyi_summary:
The day started with the filter swap removing filter U and installing filter Y, no issues reported, Petr worked on the M1M3TS, adjusting its frequency to 50 Hz and requesting a vibration check at the glycol pump near the cell. Warm-ups performed at 15:30 UTC and the Daily Calsys sequence at 16:48 UTC both completed without issues, and the dome handover was also smooth, where louvers were also tested. When preparing to take some darks in the TMA Checkouts, we found painting work taking place on Level 5, preventing us from obtaining darks in full darkness, but then Yousuke and Pierre confirmed that won't be huge issue having dome lights on when taking those darks, which are not for science purpose. Also dome lights were not possible to turn them off through the Shelly app and had to be turn off mannually. Merlin noted that all processes appeared to be running on yagan10, which raised a concern that Ivan solved it, tomorrow IT will do a physical inspection. Then, during venting at 23:09 UTC, the Dynalene flow rate dropped to zero (OBS-1416). David J remotely reset the system and restored the flow to its nominal value. In the meantime, the camera had to be powered off until the Dynalene flow stabilized.

Start-of-night was delayed slightly by the camera recovery, followed by a longer delay due to the initial alignment not working due to some configuration mismatch (OBS-1415).  We also observed some misbehaviors of the MTQueue, failing to configure scripts and failing to load schema (OBS-1414 and OBS-1417).  We were able to run just over an hour of !!!CHAOS MONKEY!!! before handing over to stray light testing, followed by the focus sweep and filter offset tests (y and z band).  Some faults with the rotator and AOS seemingly interrupted blocks in ways that confused the scheduler or script queue (and the observers!).  We could not get FBS targets into the queue with the standard configuration (OBS-1420), but the poor seeing configuration did generate targets, and we were able to end the night with just over an hour of FBS imaging.  AOS residuals were consistently in the 0.3" - 0.4" range during FBS observations.

After dome closure at 18-degree twilight, we ran the daily calibrations without issue.  The linux workstations continue to be troublesome in various ways; toward the end of the night Chrome became unresponsive and crashed on one workstation, wiping out basically all the screens needed for control and monitoring of the observatory (OBS-1421).  Otherwise a smooth end-of-night shutdown.
auxtel_summary: AuxTel daily checkouts passed with no issues and we started to vent at 17:00 UTC until it went onsky.  We closed it down at sun elevation -8.
observers_crew: Gonzalo Aravena;Alysha Shugart;Lukas Eisert;Eric Christensen;Danica Žilková

summary: Daytime ran smoothly overall, with routine warmups, software updates, and several subsystem redeployments. Petr addressed multiple FCU issues and stabilized flows. Dome operations opened as planned, and all systems proceeded normally through the evening.  Night operations were again productive despite some faults.  Major issues at shutdown with the GIS faulting M1M3 and locking up the TMA.  Parked at horizon, platforms out, ready for optics cleaning.
weather_summary:
Clear skies
Temperature averaged 15C during daytime, 12C overnight.
HUmidity 22% very consistent
windspeed ~3 m/s at sunset, rising to 8-10 m/s through the night.
simonyi_summary:
The day started with the hexapods warmup with no issues. Wouter used the OCS queue to update the Watcher to improve the low-residual-voltage alarms on the MTDome capacitor banks. The MTScheduler was restarted on Argo CD. Brian B updated the EAS and DREAM CSCs, Petr worked across multiple FCUs, swapping glycol lines, fixing leaks and valve issues (including FA108 and FA312), correcting the flowmeter pipe diameter, and stabilizing several units, while also testing higher pump speeds to improve flow. Pierre requested control of the FES to run a test, and Wouter and Amanda redeployed several ESS CSCs and their Raspberry Pi controllers. The bump test and break-away test were completed with no issues, TMA checkouts passed without problems. Louvers were opened at 22:38 UTC at 50% and dome shutters at 22:58. EAS was left on STANDBY for ~40 min.

Night crew started the initial alignment at sun elevation -10, and the system converged nicely to delivered IQ of ~0.8".  The CHAOS MONKEY test lived up to its name, scheduling fields within 20 degrees of the moon and tripping the HV on one sensor (OBS-1423).  We then tried to image stray light bananas for BLOCK-T540, but had some issues and had to abandon the block (it needs more testing on BTS).  This may have left some persistent rotator offsets (OBS-999) which were cleared with help from Tiago.  FBS observations proceeded smoothly, and the focus sweep block was also run since donut blur seeing estimates were consistently below 0.8".  Last night's issue with scripts failing to configure occurred intermittently (OBS-1414), and one instance may have triggered a slowdown in how the scheduler handles scripts (OBS-1426).  Stopped the FBS at astronomical twilight.

Dome and louvers were closed but while preparing the TMA for calibrations, there was a GIS communication loss which faulted several systems (OBS-1427).  Robinson pitched in from the hotel to recover, which took about 45 minutes to get back to a usable TMA.  The M1M3 had lowered when it faulted, and we left it lowered.  Calibrations were abandoned and the TMA was parked at horizon, platforms deployed, ready for optics cleaning day.
auxtel_summary: Manuel did some tests during the morning, then Daily checkouts were performed and at 17:00 UTC started to vent. We got an ATMCS fault which forced us to cycle all CSC in AuxTel and left it venting until it went on-sky.  AuxTel promptly sprang into action at sun elevation -8 and cranked out spectra all night long without complaint.

summary: Today was day 1 of the pre-LSST survey tests! A commercial power outage delayed the start of the survey, but once up and running it performed with minimal intervention throughout the night.
weather_summary: Clear skies the whole day. Daytime humidity was around 20% and wind speed ~6 m/s until evening. The sky was clear throughout the entire night with temperatures at a constant 12-13 °C and wind speeds increased to 9-10 m/s. Dimm Seeing ~ 0.9"
simonyi_summary:
Warmups started early in the morning without interrupting the mirror cleaning work. An apparent HVAC communication failure caused the MANs to shut down in the morning and was under investigation. The M1 louver is ready and at full performance, was validated during dome handover, and some images were taken to document the effect of opening louvers at 10% and 50% for internal sunlight reflections. After waiting for TMA handover, we completed M1M3 tests and the TMA checkout with no issues, though adjusting settings to 10% triggered an MTM1M3 interlock, sending the system and some ESS into fault; these were recovered and TMA control was restored. The dome was slewed to 90 degrees to open shutters and louvers, and ESS 107/108 remained in STANDBY until we cycled them with the mirror lowered. Tiago also recovered some MTQueue scripts that were failing due to a “configuration_failed” condition.

There was a commercial power outage that lasted 10min (Mitsubishi generator turned on). The observatory recovered the cooling system, but we were delayed from on-sky observations due to TMA and dome issues (OBS-1401 and OBS-1428; 1.5hrs lost). Once recovered, we ran the “pre-LSST” survey (i.e., a FBS-driven soak test) the whole night. For detailed comparison of the observing night with simulations, check out this USDF Times Square Notebook: 

https://usdf-rsp.slac.stanford.edu/times-square/github/lsst/schedview_notebooks/prenight/run_sim?day_obs=20251127&sim_nights=1&ts_hide_code=1. 

Most M1M3 thermal gradients show no major changes during the night, except for the Z-gradint, which diverged from its operational limits after 5:00 UTC. After a couple of MTDome faults followed by a cascade of CSC faults from a possible GIS connection issue (OBS-1428 and OBS-1427), we ended the night early (~1 hour of time loss). While attempting to do the daily calibrations, we received a connectivity error for the FiberSpectrographs (OBS-572). Given that we were approaching sunrise, we decided to instead close for the night.
auxtel_summary: Manuel performed some tests on the telescope this morning, mirror cleaning also was completed, and Patricio C rebooted the cRIO for ATMCS/ATPneumatics along with additional tests. Daily checkouts passed with no issues, and venting began at 20:00 UTC. AuxTel went on-sky around 23:30 UTC (only one ATPtg error - azimuth out of range), and surveyed the whole night.

summary: Simonyi ran a second night of it “pre-LSST” survey as well as an additional stray light test case. Morning and night operations were relatively smooth, and we ended observations with M1M3TS testing rather than daily calibrations.
weather_summary:
Clear skies and low wind at the beginning of the night. Ventilation began at a Sun elevation of –13°, with the dome closed and the louvers set to 50%, using VEC 04 to assist air circulation.

During the night, there were periods of time when the humidity jumped from 20% to around 40-50%, causing alarm over the dew-point difference with the cryo 1 hex temperature but no greater concerns.
simonyi_summary:
The telescope was moved to zenith for a glycol hose replacement in the cell during the morning. We began with the hexapods warm-ups, there was a brief power cut that only impacted the second-level lights and did not interrupt the warm-up or the Dynalene system. Daily Calsys proceeded by testing only the reflectors, as FiberSpectrograph101 had a problem to get enabled. We continued with the M1M3 bump test at 17:20 UTC, and during the dome handover we experienced a position synchronization issue caused by an EtherCAT connection; Lorenzo performed a remote reset that resolved it, and the event was added to OBS-646. We tested the new unpark_mount script, which worked flawlessly, and the louvers were opened for venting as usual, followed by the shutters opening.

We started initial alignment during nautical twilight had began the “pre-LSST” survey. We had a new issue with the MTAOS (OBS-1430) that affected the AOS quality of several images (images flagged). Around 6:00 UTC, MTScheduler CSC crashed, losing heartbeats, and went into Standby for some time before we could re-enable the Scheduler (OBS-1431; time loss ~0.75hr).

After the FBS observations, we completed the night with a stray light test case and closed the dome around 8:00 UTC (did not fully complete the stray light test). We then took IR images around the TMA, and prepared the telescope for morning M1M3 thermalization tests.
auxtel_summary: Daily checkouts started at 17:20 UTC and the system was left venting from 17:40 UTC. No issues encountered. AuxTel went on-sky at 23:45 UTC. It ran without issue the entire night.

summary: Flawless night in Simonyi and AuxTel. About 490 LSSTCam science images non-stop taken by the Scheduler.
weather_summary: Clear skies, moderate humidity (around 30%), and calm winds  (<3m/s). We began venting when the Sun was at an elevation of 12°, at which time the outside temperature was oscillating atypically, due to that we closed the louvers and wait until sun elevation -5 deg (20:50 CLT) to open completely the dome.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime 
We completed the M1M3 Thermalization Test (BLOCK-T651).
It was a very calm day with only minor system-related issues. We experienced an expected episode involving the LinearStage 104 (see OBS-1432 for details).
Another relevant point concerns the oil observed on the platform during the TMA walk-around; please refer to the FRACAS-317 for further information.

Nighttime
Flawless night. After the initial alignment FBS constrained pre-LSST was in progress (z band) with Seq.34 onward. We started with residual AOS FWHM 0.4", PSF FWHM (median) 0.9", donut blur 0.8" and, monotonic ellipticity < 0.1. Most of the night we were around the PSF FWHM (median) 0.9".
auxtel_summary:
It was a flawless performance for AuxTel.
The weekly calibrations were completed today.

summary: We lost the TMA's encoders multiple times, which caused the elevation and azimuth axes to fail. Most of the night was focused in TMA recovery and troubleshooting, unfortunately FBS observations only produced a handful of images. In the last third of the night we performed an AOS stability test on a fixed position. Average DIMM seeing 1".
weather_summary: Clear skies, moderate humidity (around 50%), and calm conditions with winds below 5 m/s. The outside temperature remained higher than the inside temperature until (19:35 CLT), when venting was initiated. RH remained between 25% to  56% throughout the night.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime
We began the day with the M1M3 Thermalization Test (BLOCK-T651), as we did yesterday. Operations were calm and free of system issues. The only relevant note is the oil found on the platform during the TMA walk-around; see FRACAS-317 for details.

Nighttime
After telescope alignment, we started the pre-LSST survey in a “degraded mode”. Not much time passed after we began the survey when we started loosing the TMA encoder heads in recurring positions, making the TMA's axes faulted. With the support of Franco C. online leads us to believe it is due to an azimuth dirty encoder tape. Tape that can only be cleaned and inspected during the daytime by the mechanical team (4h lost). The entire history of problems can be referenced in the tickets OBS-965 and FRACAS-317. On the fly, with the support of Erik D., it was decided to switch to another block at a fixed position on-sky until the end of the night: AOS BLOCK-T641 Stability test.
We finished the night with the LSSTCam Daily Calibrations.

HVAC configuration changed back to daytime configuration. VEC 04 turned OFF manually.
auxtel_summary: Flawless performance for AuxTel.

summary: Lots of TMA faults during the day, continuing from last night.  Nighttime observations were conducted in a restricted range of azimuth that seemed to avoid the TMA encoder errors (at least until parking).  AOS and FBS filled the night, but daily calibrations couldn't be completed.
weather_summary: Clear.  Wind speed ~10m/s, humidity ~15%, temperature ~11C in the morning. Wind goes down towards ~3m/s and humidity rose to ~50-60% during the afternoon and overnight.
simonyi_summary:
We ran hexapods warm ups in the morning, and daily calsys checkouts after lunch. Dome handover done at 15:55, while we rotated the TMA for encoder tape cleaning at the same time, as requested by Freddy. After the tailgate meeting, we ran some TMA motion test for encoder robustness, where MTMount faults frequently at ~AZ=+-57 (OBS-965). We decided to run observations with fixed  pointing or restricted AZ range tonight. After dinner, we ran M1M3 bump test and hard points test before opening the dome. We met MTmount fault (elevation axis fault, OBS-1233) and OSS fault while opening the dome (obs-1267). We opened the louvers, enabled dimms and recovered OSS before transition to night crew.

Initial alignment went well but we ran into some difficulty with the correct_pointing script (OBS-1434) which extended the alignment time somewhat.  BLOCK-T648 Chaos Monkey proved difficult to tame tonight, first over-perturbing the optical state, then waiting nearly an hour between perturbations instead of the desired 30 minutes.  We completed 3 steps of the filter offset tests, for i, z, and g-bands.  Finished the night with about an hour of scheduler-driven observations.

Calibration setup was delayed by the dome spinning 360 degrees when commanded to go to a place where it already was (OBS-1435).  We got the cal screen aligned with the laser, but then daily calibrations were defeated by both FiberSpectrographs being wedged (OBS-1436).  MTMount faulted when sending the TMA into the danger zone, faulting at +57.3 azimuth (OBS-965).  Observer workstations continue to be problematic, with Chronograf failing to load more than one dashboard on workstation02 today(OBS-1433).
auxtel_summary: Auxtel daytime checkouts finished successfully and venting stated early in the day.  AuxTel observed all night and closed without issue.
observers_crew: Kate Napier;Shuang Liang;Karla Pena;Eric Christensen;Erik Dennihy;Bryce Kalmbach

summary:
The day started with the unresolved encoder issue we have faced for the past couple days which prevented us from running the full azimuth range of pre-LSST FBS observations last night (OBS-965).  Issue seems temporarily resolved.  At night, we ran AOS and stray light tests, with FBS observations rounding out the night.  Calibrations were done in the morning, and the TMA is parked at zenith.

Please note: the lights inside the PFlow were left on, and were shut off by the Late crew an hour after the start of the night.
weather_summary: Clear.  Maximum daytime temperature ~19 deg C leading to a warmer night (14C).  Humidity and wind stayed low.  Atmosphere was a little more unsettled than last night with seeing in the 1-1.2" range.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime checkouts went smoothly with the exception of FiberSpectrograph.101 and 102 failing to enable during the calibration system checkout (OBS-1436).  After yesterday's azimuth slew tests designed to uncover the cause of the encoder issues, it was revealed that az = 90 and az = 270 deg were the most likely problematic areas.  This morning, Kate and Freddy spent time inspecting these azimuths and found weakened joints underneath the OSS tray that are leaking oil onto the encoder tape below (see updated photos and videos in OBS-965).       

The TMA walkaround was completed earlier in the day than normal to allow time for further afternoon encoder testing.  The azimuth slew tests confirmed that az = 90 deg was problematic, and after Freddy cleaned this area again, the subsequent azimuth slews had no issues.  We are now cleared to run the TMA at the full range of azimuths tonight.

Initial alignment, pointing correction and start of the AOS tests went well, though the night was warmer than predicted so the M1M3 thermal system took a while to settle.  The Chaos Monkey block was run for just over 1.5 hours, followed by successful stray light ghost hunting and filter offset tests (all filters available).  The night ended with FBS-driven observations until astronomical twilight.

Setting up for calibrations took some extra time due to an unnecessary 360-degree spin of the dome (OBS-1435) and a TMA timeout likely coincident with a dropped encoder (OBS-965).  But calibrations were taken without issue and the TMA parked at zenith as requested.
auxtel_summary: AuxTel checkouts completed in the morning.  AuxTel vented from 13:20 UTC until we began on-sky observations at 8-degree twilight.  Shortly before going on sky, ATSpectrograph faulted but was quickly recovered (OBS-1438).  One recurrence of an old minor fault (OBS-342) was also quickly resolved.  Otherwise a smooth night.
observers_crew: Kate Napier;Shuang Liang;Karla Pena;Eric Christensen;Erik Dennihy;Bryce Kalmbach

summary: Smooth day and night filter offset testing. We only missed the last LUT version due to time constraints.
weather_summary: Night started with 50% humidity and minimal winds, was an increase of temperature from 13 to 15 degrees around 05:46 UTC. and that resulted in a worst seeing conditions.
simonyi_summary:
First half of the day was dedicated M1M3 cell work and, filter work and tours. Major daytime activities included FA314 replacement and TMA Az encoder tests (at 5% and 20% perfromance settings). Tonight, is the first night with 20%. We discovered a potential link between TMA home-ing script and high HP forces on M1M3-- still in development! We had a recurrence of the old issue where CCW is not tracking rotator after recovering the MTPtg from a fault. 

We were able to vent the dome early in the evening with louvers at around 20 deg solar elevation.

Most of the night was dedicated to the BLOCK-T559, where we found two problems that were quickly resolved. The first was high network traffic causing the MTCamera CSC to fault (OBS-1441). No action was taken; the problem resolved itself.

The second problem appeared when starting FBS: the CCW limit switches/pull cord alarms (OBS-875), which was resolved according to the documentation. After resolving the problem, FBS was able to run for 15 minutes with TMA set to 20% speed, most of the FBS slews showed HP maximum forces greater than 700N, with about 25% exceeding 1000N.

We finish with daily calibrations, we propose to Modify the BLOCK-T399 to save some time (OBS-1442).
auxtel_summary: Smooth sailing!

summary: Relatively smooth during the day. Dome hand over took a bit longer due to extra request to restart cRIO.  AOS and stray light on sky before a sudden spike in humidity forced an early close.  Closed-dome stray light investigations finished the night.
weather_summary: High humidity during the day up to 65%. Low wind, warm in the day but temperatures started falling towards sunset.  Overnight, humidity oscillated significantly, and some wispy clouds blew through in the second half of the night.  At 6:30 UTC temperatures dropped by 2C over ~10 minutes and humidity spiked to 78%.
simonyi_summary:
EIE work during the day as usual. Daily checkouts went smooth. Dome handover at 3:30 PM CLT, but with additional request from Te-Wei to restart the Dome cRIO. It took us several tries to correctly restart the cRIO and home the dome (lessons: STANDBY the mount before restarting cRIO; use home_dome with readings from the wall marker as input for physical_az). We tried the new unpark_mount script and it works amazing. After dinner we ran the TMA AZ test again but at 5%, as requested by David J.

We started venting from about 20:00 UTC with partially open louvers.

On-sky startup went smoothly, but it took a while for the seeing to stabilize enough to run the AOS filter offset block (LUT v0).  RubinTV/RA was sluggish to update but was quickly fixed (OBS-1444).  Next were some stray light investigations, and then back to AOS filter offsets (LUT v7, again).  We were interrupted by an MTMount azimuth encoder fault (OBS-1445), and then by a chorus of humidity alarms which forced the dome closed more than an hour earlier than planned.  We did not finish the v7 LUT and no FBS observations were done.

We set up for an in-dome stray light investigation with the CBP, but could only finish one of three steps (setup and execution time of BLOCK-T610 is very underestimated).  Daily calibrations were skipped.
auxtel_summary: A few tests done by Manuel in the morning. The night otherwise was smooth!

simonyi_summary:

summary: Today was full of clear skies and smooth operations. Night was majority AOS testing with a couple of other short tests incorporated throughout. Camera cryo trim heat was lower than previous nights, but we observed the whole night regardless.

 Mild winds between 2-7 m/s

simonyi_summary:
— Daytime Summary — EAS enabled to default configuration ~ 12:36 UTC

FiberSpectrograph:103 re-started during the day, daily calsys checkout 2nd attempt passed. It seems we had a dome network issue that affected the LEDProjector, LinearStages CSCs, along with ESS.107 and ESS.108 reported in OBS-1189. 

We run the TMA Az encoders head test (BLOCK-T657), this time Az encoder head 4 faulted at Az ~ -17 deg. Earlier when moving the TMA we Az head 1 faulted at Az ~97 deg. 

Additional minor faults during the day reported in OBS-1197 and OBS-979.

— Nighttime Summary —
We started venting at -6deg sun elevation due to higher temperatures (EAS M1M3TS was disabled >30min due to stable thermal gradients). Initial alignment started at astronomical twilight, and we spent the beginning of the night with Check Filter LUT Offsets AOS test (r —> i). In between, we also ran pointing model and TARTS tests. The TMA azimuth axis faulted in the middle of the night (OBS-958 and OBS-959), losing ~20min of observing time.

At around 6:45 UTC, the cryo trim heat dropped below 10W (cryo 3 was left on overnight), but we were approved to continue with observing until closure. We ended the night with the hexapod compensation mode test and daily calibrations.
auxtel_summary: AuxTel daily checkouts passed, started venting around 12 pm today. On-sky procedures went smoothly, and AuxTel observed the whole night without issue.

summary:
Warm night with low Cryo Trim Heat <10W. Except of this inconvenience, it was a smooth night for Simonyi and AuxTel.

At 6:41 UTC we felt an earthquake which left its marks in the measured HP Forces but did not fail anything.
weather_summary:
clear skies, no clouds during the day, daytime temp averaged ~15°C, humidity ~40% and windspeed about 1m/s by the evening.
At dome opening (0:10 UTC) temperature outside was still 12.88 deg and refusing to significantly drop. Inside temperature 11.77 deg. Only after 4 UTC the outside temp reached 12.5 deg.
simonyi_summary:
The main day time actives included -- filter swap (y --> u), natural frequency sequencer testing for Camera and dynalene system update. The filter swap took all morning. Dynalene updates were attempted and continued after lunch, but were aborted. The camera team carried out new firmware/sequencer testing, and the observers help acquire 100 biases (5 sec with 1s pause). RA struggled to catch up but it went fine. More bias acquisitions had to be aborted due RCE restarts causing some issues. The team returned the Camera to its nominal configuration for on-sky operations. 

The M1M3 hardpoint and force actuator bump tests were skipped today. Regular checks included hexapod warm-ups, filter change exercise and TMA and camera checkouts. The Calsys checkouts had issues enabling LinearStage104; which was later resolved by Eric Coughlin and we were able to complete the test. The dome handover was completed at 19:00 UTC with no issues, and the TMA checkouts passed successfully. Scheduler 1 was restarted in ArgoCD today due to memory issues.

Dome started venting at 0:10 UTC. During Venting we encountered an issue with the Camera trim heat sinking to 2.23W which urged us to lower the TMA to 32 deg to recover the Cryo. Despite this we started initial alignment at El 60 deg at 0:40 UTC. During this, the Trim Heat stabilized at 4W. 

After this we run BLOCK-T288 pointing model at El 60. Then 656 (Hexapod Compensation Mode Test), 660 (AOS Overall focus offset). We reran T656 twice because Tiago was not satisfied with the results of the first run. During this time, the Trim Heat stayed close to 2W and climbed up to 7W. We tested the Pointing Model with Tiago (T513) and spend the last hour with FBS (T655). 
At 7:44 UTC the Rotator got too old Telemetry from the CCW and failed which we took as a proper reason to close for the night, 
Daily calibrations were made and we left the observatory at 9:10 UTC.
Overall it was a good night,
auxtel_summary:
All checkouts passed with no issues, AuxTel is venting and waiting to go on-sky. AuxTel observations starting at 0:14 UTC.
Auxtel observations stopping at 07:55 UTC. Smooth night without any issues.

summary:
The day’s most important task was recovering the camera condition, enabling a smooth night overall. Venting delays due to warm temperatures shifted opening to Sun –6°, and operations ran successfully with the Hexapods using the V22 LUT. A late MTRotator–MTPtg fault was recovered, allowing survey observations to resume.

Please note that the lights on the 3rd floor and in the pFlow area remained on throughout the night. These lights must be turned off during nighttime operations. Instructions on how to switch them off are requested.
weather_summary:
Clear skies no clouds
Temps averaged ~14°C until evening
humidity ~25% during daytime and ~10% by the evening
windspeed ~2 m/s

Higher winds (up to 7 m/s) developed late in the night, along with colder temperatures and elevated, variable humidity reaching a peak of 70%.
simonyi_summary:
We started the morning with the hexapod warm-ups. Meanwhile, cabling work was carried out inside the M1M3 cell throughout the day. The daily Calsys checkouts passed with no issues. The cell work concluded around the dome handover, which was completed successfully at 19:00 UTC. TMA was handed over to us 19:26 UTC. M1M3 was raised after successful FA bump tests & Hardpoint breakaway tests at 20:00 UTC. We left the TMA immediately at horizon to recover the dramatically failing Cryo system of Camera. We managed to salvage the camera trim-heat capacity to 15-30 W. Around this time, OSS went to fault due to possibly insuffcient oil levels. It was recovered ~3 hrs later (lack of alarms to alert observers and MTMount was not in OCS control at the time). It was successfully turned on at 22:27 UTC. Dome was slewed to Az=90° and we started to wait for better conditions to start venting.

Nighttime-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

It was a smooth night overall, with only minor issues. We began by checking the camera and completing the remaining filter-change exercises carried over from the afternoon.

Venting was delayed due to warm temperatures outside the dome. We opened at a Sun elevation of –6°, and the first alignment was performed at –12°. The system ran all night using the Hexapods with the V22 LUT, as BLOCK-T395 confirmed that the LUT was performing well.

Near the end of the night, an MTRotator fault triggered an MTPtg fault. Both were recovered, and Simonyi LSSTCam Feature-Based Scheduler LSST Survey (Cons) observations were resumed. At the very end (calibrations) we got a TMA soft motion axes fault, that was recovered and calibrations resumed (before the laser tracker screen alignment).
auxtel_summary:
During the morning, the AuxTel mirror and the filter wheel were cleaned, filter wheel continued until after midday. The DIMM 2 mirror was also cleaned. We repeated the daily checkouts, which passed with no issues, and AuxTel was left venting at 18:48 UTC.

Smooth night operations without faults.

summary:
We started with the expectation of closed dome due to rain but ended with the first on-sky observations until the beginning of nautical twilight! (i.e. -12 deg sun elevation)

Night was overall calm, seeing ~1.1 arcsec and above.
No larger issues, only AuxTel had some issues which took some on-sky time.
weather_summary:
Mostly clear skies during the day. Temperature ~12°C, humidity ~50%, and wind speed ~2 m/s by the evening.
Although rain and thunder were predicted, the night was exceptionally clear with low humidity around 15% for most of the night.
At the start of the night, we had a delivered image quality of around 1 arcsec which gradually worsened to 1.35 arcsec towards 05:30 UTC. The DIMM even reported 1.5 arcsec, reliability is to be questioned because of the very low winds tonight.
simonyi_summary:
We started the day with the hexapods warm-up in the morning before the mirror cleaning, followed by the Daily Calsys, which passed with no issues.  The M1M3 bump and hard point tests were skipped today. Dome handover began at 18:50 UTC and TMA Checkouts were completed after that. Also, today Luis V had the work of switching the cold glycol supply over to the auxiliary piping, which required further cleaning.  This triggered some Dynalene alerts along with the increasing of temperature of the camera. We commented this to Luis V and we started to work together on this, and he finished around 01:00 UTC. We started venting the dome at 23:15 UTC. During this time we noticed the dome was reporting the parking position of Az 328, even though it was actually at Az 90, so we checked that at 22:17 UTC we experienced an outage with the communications to Embargo, which caused IPSec to go down. At 22:38 UTC, this possibly caused the MTDome status to change from STOPPED to PARKED and show the wrong position. 

Initial alignment started at 0:36 UTC. After this we ran the Camera LUT (BLOCK-T395), The Hexapod Compensation Mode Test (BLOCK-T656) and the Filter LUT Offset Test (BLOCK-T559). During the latter we had to deal with MTRotator getting old Telemetry from the CCW (OBS-922) which delayed the tests a bit. We then moved on to BLOCK-T614 because the delivered image quality (also the standardized one) was worse than 1.1 arcsec. The last half hour before closing at 8:30UTC was filled with the constrained FBS BLOCK-T655.  After closing we performed the Daily Calibrations which ended at ...
auxtel_summary:
Daily checkouts were performed in the morning and venting started at 13:23 UTC. When going on sky, we had the issue that the mount ignored commands to slew and timed out. First cycling ATMCS and ATPtg and then running AuxTel checkouts solved the issue. No observing time lost because of this. At 3:51 UTC the Focal Plane of ATCamera got stuck in Integrating (OBS-1286). This took away 30min of on-sky time.

During the early night we also discovered that aux-brick01.cp.lsst.org is complaining about low disk space. We cleared some space but this might not solve the issue for long. There was a discussion to bring this ominous but crucial machine under the control of the devops team in the future.

summary: Clear night with good seeing. Observations interrupted for >1 hour due to an FES fault and a meltdown of AT at the end of the night.
weather_summary:
Clear skies towards the evening. Temperatures ~11.4°C in the evening. Windspeed ~5.5 m/s
Humidity ~48% at the beginning of sunset but rapidly fell down to 20% and then stayed rather low during the night. Seeing was good with delivered image quality of around 0.8 arcsec in r/i band for most of the night.
simonyi_summary:
The day started with the hexapods warm-up in the morning along with Calsys checkouts. During dome handover, a fault occurred while testing the dome shutters; after several drive reset attempts, Gonzalo M switched the system to local mode to test them, then returned it to remote mode and it worked properly. TMA checkouts began at 19:10 UTC, but then we had a mirror cover deploying fault followed by an MTMount fault and an OSS fault at 19:24 UTC (OBS-1453), which was recovered after about one hour. After the OSS recovery, TMA checkouts and filter exercises were repeated and passed successfully. We opened the louvers and dome at 23:15 UTC (Sun el = 3.8 deg). Regarding the strategy for opening the louvers with respect to the direction from the Sun, we think better instructions are needed so that sunlight from the louvers does not hit the telescope (Discussions ongoing in the Slack channel, #rso-observing-blocks).
Initial alignment was finished at 1:10 UTC, and we continued with the stray light test BLOCK-T506. After this we did the Hartmann Camera Offset Test BLOCK-T663 without any issues. But then: when starting with BLOCK-T559 Check Filter LUT Offsets, MTCamera faulted because of an FES error reported in OBS-1454. This problem was escalated first to Sean and then to Pierre who thankfully were able to solve the issue after 1.3h. At 4:20 UTC, we were back on sky finally conducting the block. This test was performed until Step 11 when we closed at 08:36 UTC. IR camera Walkaround around the TMA (BLOCK-T647) was finished at 9:45 UTC and we left the observatory with the M1M3 Thermalization Step Test Case BLOCK-T650.
auxtel_summary:
Daytime checkouts done in the morning and venting started at 14:30 UTC. Observations started at 00:20 UTC.
The night was smooth until 6:55 UTC when ATMCS did not accept any commands anymore. Furthermore we were not able to close the Mirror covers as also ATPneumatics did not respond. We solved the issue with a cRIO restart and were able to shutdown AuxTel gracefully for the night (OBS-1455).

summary:
An unrecoverable problem with the OSS stemming from Chiller 2 prevented us from observing with Simonyi, either on sky or in closed dome.  Ian O. will go to the summit early Sunday morning to recover Chiller 2.

High humidity prevented us from observing until 05:40 UTC.  Given the aforementioned OSS problem which prevented any Simonyi observing, we were only able to observe with AuxTel.
weather_summary: At the end of the day thick clouds started forming and humidity raised above 70%. We didn't achieve safe observing conditions until after 05:30 UT.
simonyi_summary:
During the day, there was work done - glycol filter cleaning, checking Chiller 1 glycol, and installation of brackets for dome environment monitoring on louvers E1 and H1. Later in the afternoon, MTMount faulted causing a TMA Interlock: OSS Alarm, but OSS was not in fault state. However, there was an Alarm on Chiller 2 on L1 which was not possible to acknowledge - issue linked to OBS-1462. We also found some water stains on the floor below Chiller 1 and 2 - OBS-1461. We proceeded with restarting the OSS and continuing Chiller 2 in alarm state with no power. 

Franco remotely supported OSS troubleshooting for a couple hours, but ultimately, Chiller 2 could not be recovered.  With just Chiller 1, the capacity was quite limited and the OSS would fault after 30 minutes. Electronics team advised that the TMA was not safe to use during the night, and we made the decision to point the TMA at the calibration screen.  We were only able to run whitelight flats in the i-band.
auxtel_summary: AuxTel daytime checkouts went fine and we started venting. When the humidity rose above 70%, we closed AuxTel at around 21:45 UTC.  At 05:40 UTC, the humidity had dropped low enough for us to observe with AuxTel for the remainder of the night.

summary: There was high humidity at the start of the night, but around 01:00 UTC it had decreased enough for on-sky observing.  Simonyi observed with the FBS for the remainder of the night, and there were no issues with AuxTel. We saw a few minor errors during FBS obs, including the EAS frequently faulting and a CCW error, but minimal time was lost.
weather_summary: Daytime temperature was ~ 10 C, ~ 9 m/s wind speed, and it was more humid during the day than yesterday. The humidity rose so fast after 21:30 UTC, peaking at 83%. The temperature dropped down to 6.5 C and settled around 7 deg C for the rest of the night. The rise in humidity followed by a decrease has been the trend of the last few days.
simonyi_summary:
Even though it was Sunday and holiday in Chile, it was a very productive day on the summit today. 

In the morning, Ian E. O. came up to summit from La Serena (before voting, thank you so much Ian!) and checked Chiller 2 and the OSS. CHILLER 2 WAS BACK ONLINE at 13:00 UTC. Once we arrived at the control room, calibration systems were all ENABLED and blue lights shone in the dome camera. We checked them during the TMA walk around, and finally turned off the lights after daily calsys checkouts.  We figured out that it was the whitelight for i-band flats from the last night. After this, we performed M1M3 tests for preparing in-dome test in the afternoon. There have been several unpark_mount.py faults with MTMount fault for last 3 days (OBS-1464).

We had several MTPtg faults with "Motion locked" during home_both_axes. It seems it was locked at 2:47 UTC and never unlocked until we unlocked MTMount and MTRotator motion locks (OBS-1465). TMA Tests finished and passed. M1M3 mini in-situ wash done with convincing results. This said we found more waterdrops under the TMA (which was at Horizon) indicating further dripping water pools at the TMA. Our leading theory are still the cold uncovered Dynalene lines at the TMA and TEA. Some initial insulating work was performed at the Dynalene lines at the Topring. Furthermore the setpoint of the Dynalene Chiller to 2 deg. During that we also switched from Chiller 2 to Chiller 1. This switch caused the camera to warm up, and to a shutdown of the CCDs, because Chiller 1 was not actually cooling the Dynalene. Because of that we returned to Chiller 2. The change lead initially to a supply with 2 deg cold dynalene. However the PDI control of the setpoint caused large oscillations in the output temperature which was not acceptable for the safety of the camera. We finally returned to the original -1 deg setpoint which stabilized the situation (Details in OBS-1490).

---Nighttime log---
Overview: 
There was a discussion for opening the dome in the sense of inside/outside dew point between OSs and Com-Sci (OBS-1479). There are inside dew point sensors in TEA, and near camera and they shows higher dew points than outside dew point temperature, which we used as a guide to avoid condensation on TEA. While the discussion was on-going, outside dew point dropped down quickly from 01:20 UTC (but still varies a lot) and eventually reached to -10 C (delta > 12 C) at 1:40 UTC. We opened the dome at 01:43 UTC but before that, we did visual inspection to check water drops or condensations on TMA, and we couldn't find any special liquid part. After the initial alignment, we ran FBS for the whole night, because DIMM seeing was ~ 1.1 to 1.3". After MTPtg and MTRotator FAULT (OBS-673) at 08:22 UTC, we just stop the scheduler and shutdown the Simonyi. We closed dome and louvers 08:35 UTC.

After closing dome, we did visual inspection again at the end of the night during walkaround with IR camera (BLOCK-T647).  

*Issues: 
Over the night, there were several Dome Az errors occurred but easily recovered by exitFault. There was another issue that enable_aos_closed_loop.py script not configured well during FBS was running. That recovered after re-suming scheduler twice from Tiago's recommendation. This seems not script issue but more like IT issue, Tiago said. There was one more event but simply we fixed issue by adding the same script on the top of the script queue and removing the unsuccessfully configured one. There were MTPtg, MTRotator FAULT at the end of the night (OBS-673). ESS:118 went to FAULT after closing dome and couldn't bring it back to ENABLED (OBS-1496).

*BLOCKS we ran:
   *BLOCK-T539 (Initial Alignment) : 02:39 UTC - 03:32 UTC
   *BLOCK-T655 (FBS - good seeing) : 03:35 UTC - 08:23 UTC
   *BLOCK-T647 (Dome Walkaround with IR Camera) : 08:50 UTC - 09:20 UTC

---Daytime log---
No work in the dome. We did a quick walk around in the morning, and we found a lot of oil leak (OBS-1494) and a tiny puddle of water on the ground (OBS-1479). Hexapods and Calsys checkouts done smoothly. After lunch we unparked the TMA, where we saw TMA faults (OBS-1495).     * We did follow-up inspections and discovered two other areas that were producing condensation. Pictures included on the same log post.
* At 2:26 UTC we had to recover another dynalene failure (details in FRACAS-823).

Other OBS tickets reported (no significant time loss):

During the TMA walk-around at 15:48 UTC we found new liquid stains (oily and pinkish hue) on the azimuth platform and under the TEA (-X side/ left side of M1M3), which were most likely there from last night. simonyi_summary:
— Nighttime Summary —
* Due to high condensation on the exposed dynalene pipes (OBS-1479), we did not go on-sky tonight (weather time loss 8hrs). However, the condensation was low enough to run in-dome calibration tests for the night.
* We parked the TMA at an irregular azimuth (-212deg rather than 148deg). 
    * The reason is we are moving the TMA at 5% speed to minimize condensation falling. 
    * This will also allow the daytime OS team to inspect the areas that have condensation, but also minimize the travel distance to and from the calibration screen.

Observing Plan During Night:
* BLOCK-T382 (LSSTCam Super Biases): 23:44 — 3:05 UTC.
* BLOCK-T563 (PTC Curve — 750 Pairs): 3:43 — 8:30 UTC.
    * The +X M1M3 mirror cover was still stuck (OBS-1497), and will require work from the day crew on Monday. All data taken for this block has the caveat of only three out of four mirror covers retracted.
        * Due to the mirror cover issue, we intentionally delayed the start of this block to prioritize taking biases since this data will not be sufficient for the PTC.
        * We also did not align the TMA to the calibration screen with the laser tracker.
    * At 7:10 UTC, M1M3 faulted due to an unexpected activated interlock on the mirror cell door (OBS-1498, 0.53hrs lost for recovery).

— Daytime Summary —
There was a fault of M1M3, M1M3 TS and SS in the morning, recovered by Petr K., and TS setpoints were set to 10/11C. In the morning we inspected the condensations on Dynalene pipes - there were water drops forming on all the non-insulated components. In preparation for the LSSTCam new firmware tests, we had to move to the calibration screen. Therefore, we decided to move slowly higher in elevation and inspect the water condensations. Some water dropped on the mirror covers, but just few water lines formed which were drying quickly, so we decided to move to el. 45, raise the mirror, move to calibration screen and open mirror covers. After the movement, there were some water marks on the mirror, but mostly old ones. One of the mirror covers X+ did not retract most likely due to a hardware issue. We completed the Daily Calsys Checkouts and Hexapods Warm-ups to prepare for the Camera tests. David J. M. raised the Dynalene setpoint by 1 degree to help battle the condensations. David J. M. also rebooted the TMA PXI trying to recover the stuck mirror cover, however unsuccessfully. During the TMA reboot, Camera Hexapod faulted, most likely linked to reported ticket OBS-449. After TMA recovery, we recovered the Hexapod as well and were ready to do the Camera tests (with one mirror cover deployed).

During morning TMA inspections we saw that the condensations on Dynalene pipes decreased. The outside humidity was ~30% and dew point was <0C, while inside it was >2C, so we decided to vent the dome for 20 minutes with louvers opened to 30% - this dried the dome completely. There were no condensations and inside dome dew point decreased below 0C. We were able to move the TMA to 75 deg el., open the mirror covers and perform all the checkouts and warm-ups. There were several faults of M1M3TS which required a CSC restart and cRIO reboot, but Petr K. recovered everything by the evening. There were also two faults of the EAS, probably linked to TS faults (OBS-1377). In the evening we moved the telescope to the calibration screen and prepared for the Camera tests. Evening visual inspection of the TMA showed no new condensation, although the outside and inside dew point increased to 5.3C and 4.3C respectively.

Nightime operations started with PTC Curve BLOCK-T563 at 00:14 UTC and ran it for the rest of the night.
- We had two M1M3TS CSC faults. Related to an Unknown EGW pump error 5000 (OBS-1344), but were recovered just by cycling the component. 
- Then at 08:44 UTC MTCamera went to fault state marking a retrieval fail in the image 1093 (OBS-1499). We cleared the error and ran again the PTC Curve.
- There was also a FiberSpectrograph fault with a message of 'Bad Gateway', which stopped the scriptqueue again.

Today, Kevin F. and Cristian A. inspected the Top End Assembly and found water puddles (approximately 1 liter). The team dried the water before the day crew departed. After discussing the situation in the tailgate meeting and on Slack (#summit-simonyi), we agreed that if one or more temperature sensors are within 2°C of the dew point, we will keep the TMA at horizon to reduce the risk of water leaking into the camera. To mitigate this risk, David J. increased Dynalene Chiller #2 setpoint from 1°C to 2°C.

Checking mirror cover X+ (OBS-1497) remains pending, its location is not accessible without removing some covers

——— Nighttime  ——— 

The dome was opened at 00:25 UTC and initial alignment started at 00:56 UTC. During alignment, we noticed an increase in temperature of the m1m3, and in the inside cell was colder than above the mirror and the outside temperature. Therefore, since the night was warmer this night than the previous night, the mirror temperature rose while the cell attempted to stay cold due to the cold glycol setpoint being at much lower temperature. Followed by a M1M3TS connection faults with the glycol system (cannot communicate with the EGW pump). All this problem affected the quality of the images so, as a result, we set M1M3TS to STANDBY and EAS was enabled using the disable configuration. Afterward, mirror temperatures stabilized, but due to poor seeing (>1,3") we switched to the FBS poor-seeing BLOCK-T630. Later in the night, as the seeing improved, we changed back to start with the BLOCK-T667_v3 LUT.

simonyi_summary:
------------ Night Time --------------
OSS Chiller errors were recovered at 22:14 UTC (It took ~ 3 hours).

OSS operated from 22:14 to 05:39 UTC (7 hours 25 mins). 

There were repeated HVAC Chiller2 alarm too. We contacted with electrical team, and they can fix it tomorrow when people come up here because of connection issue on VPN. 

At 04:08 UTC, we had ESS:114-117 FAULT and recovered them.

Around 6:30 UTC, night OS crew left the observatory due to the backup OS suffering mental/physical exhaustion during the night. For context, they had to drive themselves to the observatory in the early afternoon with nearly zero resting time once they arrived, so they were not in the best condition to work an entire night shift. This early departure was given approval by Kevin Reil.

The other OS spent the remainder of the night at Hotel Pachon monitoring the camera subsystems.

------------ Day Time ----------------
Camera leak detection still going on. Stuart managed to seal (temporarily) the leak with alcohol, cryo pressure down to 2e-8 torr (as low as the turbo pump can do). We'll keep monitoring the pressure as alcohol evaporates in the next few days.

M2 ESS work done by David, Wouter and Ian.

We encountered a brief power cut at dinner time. Both power generator ran for 10 minutes and glycol/dynalene cut off for ~1 munite. Glycol flow at chiller 02 stayed low after the cut. OSS faulted due to the power cut (time out powering on the BoschPowerSupply).

Command failed on vent gate and extraction fan (OBS-1567), but they are closed on built-in safety mechanism due to the power cut.

simonyi_summary:

* Monitored the cryo vacuum and dynalene systems. Both remained stable throughout the entire night.
    * Cryo vacuum reached a minimum of 1.86e-7 (1:18 UTC) and slowly began to climb.
    * By 6:37 UTC, the vacuum leveled out to 1.89e-7 before it turned over and  started decreasing again.
* We also ran the OSS from 1:17 — 3:25 UTC, and no issues appeared during its operation and shutdown.
    * We had to restart  Chiller #1 twice from level 1 before we could fully turn on the OSS.

Observing Plan During Night:
* BLOCK-T679: Dome venting - louver configuration test (23:30 — 4:32 UTC).
    * Wind was lower than expected for this test (2-4 m/s), but we ran it regardless.
    * Dome shutter was facing east the entirety of this test.
    * After finishing the test, we noticed that VEC-04 was off the whole time.  Usually it turns on automatically when the wind speeds are below 5 m/s.
* BLOCK-T681: Thermal gradient with respect to dome test (4:45 — 8:55 UTC).
    * Dome was pointed at 328 deg, 238 deg, 148 deg, and 58 deg.
    * VEC-04 was turned on for this test.
    * Azimuth drives went into fault while the dome was in motion (OBS-646).
* Closed MTDome by 9:00 UTC.


-- Daytime --
Camera work continues. TMA parked at horizon, running the standard M2 Hexapod Warm-Ups and Bump Test. TMA El Limit + Interlock and Random ETPB Interlock has been cleared today by Ian E. O. and David J. M.. M1M3-IS bypasses set last weekend were released. TMA default settings were set to 5% in the EUI by Tiago R. OSS Chiller leak on L1 had been inspected and will be evaluated further tomorrow. OSS was turned on for couple of hours. Shortly after turning on the OSS faulted with Active Interlocks which must be cleared by Electronics. 23:09 the outside temperature dropped below inside dome and we are starting BLOCK-T679.

    * Dome was pointed at 328 deg, 148 deg, 58 deg, and 238 deg.
    * HVAC was in daytime configuration since the dome shutters were closed.

    * Dome was parked for this test.
* Closed MTDome by 8:45 UTC.
* From 8:48 — 9:45 UTC we were attempting to recover the TMA from a ETPB and El lim + interlock, but we were unsuccessful before finishing our shift (see OBS-1511 for details).
    * M1M3 and M1M3TS CSCs were left in STANDBY since they are affected by the GIS interlock.
 

-- Daytime --
Busy day with lot of work and updates: Consdb database had been updated by Brian B., electronics team did AUX PXI Network interface swapping for accessing test (Te-Wei T., Julen) and EL Drive sensors identification test. IT was working on re-configuring UPS (ESS: 303) IP addresses and network change on the power-dp01.cp.lsst.org device. Vibration measurements were carried out on the Mitsubishi generator (ESS: 305) and on the Caterpillar generator in locked mode (ESS: 306). OSS local/admin modes were tested by David J. M.. M1M3 TS was restarted in CRIO because it was producing too many logs. FiberSpectrographs 101 and 102 were not showing heartbeats because the docker containers in the controllers had wrong permissions - issue fixed by Amanda I.. Beginning of the evening Parker F. was working on the Laser Tracker with Fritz M. and was given priority over dome tests due to limited time on the summit.

weather_summary: Wind speed peaking 8 m/s around 17 UT. Pretty high temperatures during the day reaching 19C at 19.20 UT.  Temperature and wind dropped just a few degrees and a few m/s as the night went on.  8% humidity.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime:
During the warm-up we spotted M2 high frequency oscillations in the motor current of strut 6 and in the y-position (approximately +/-2um) during x-position testing. It seems that the oscillations were present also, at least, in the last two days (OBS-1587).
Camera wise at 17:15 UT, all REBs were turned on without issues. At around 17:18 UT we started to see a response in cryo vacuum pressure, after 1h it reached a steady value of 1.6 e-8 Torr.

Nighttime:
Night operations consisted of running the OSS for 4 hours (no issues) and executing dome thermal tests BLOCK-T679 and BLOCK-T681.  The TMA elevation is erroneously reporting -33 degrees since the end of last night (OBS-381).  The TMA az/el thermal systems were found to be in fault, and could not be recovered (OBS-1590). Dome and louvers worked without issues.
auxtel_summary:
Nominal daytime operations worked without issues.  AuxTel operated flawlessly all night.

DIMM.1 worked all night long.  DIMM.2 did not work at all and could not be transitioned out of FAULT state (OBS-1589).

summary:
Simonyi: Dome tests only. AuxTel: Observations run smoothly until the end when the dome failed to close.

We couldn’t see any of the Unifi cameras for a few hours (OBS-1188)
weather_summary:
Cool-ish day with ~17C, minimal winds and moderate humidity.

At night, mostly clear skies, temperature ranged from 14–15 °C. Humidity ranged from  45% - 10%
Mild winds < 5 m/s.
simonyi_summary:
---- daytime -----
Calm day with usual checkouts (M2 Hexapod, dome and OSS). Camera progressing well and getting ready for the pump cart removal + testing tomorrow alongside the TMA. The main activities on Camera side included turning on the ion pumps and shutting off the Turbo pump.

OSS ran from 21:26–03:13 UTC.

——— Nighttime  ——— 

Dome Test:
* BLOCK-T681 v2: Thermal gradient with respect to the dome position test. Winds ~ 1-4m/s. Run twice during the night.
auxtel_summary:
Took weekend calibrations and observed the night without any issues. During shgutdown dome did not closed (OBS-1595). We are going to manually close.


DIMM.1 was not taking data (OBS-1592), recovered 3:37 UTC by Brian S. But stopped taking data again at 4:37 UTC (OBS-1594).
DIMM.2 remains in FAULT state, and has been out of order since Feb 11 (OBS-1589)

summary: Engineering tests were focused on bring back all the systems controlling their impact in the LSSTCam cryo vacuum pressure. Once we saw no impact we point focus in take calibrations for the rest of the night. For the night time operations was not possible to take the calibrations but instead Super Biases were completed.
weather_summary: Low wind speed (2 m/s) and humidity around 30-40%. Clear skies.
simonyi_summary:
----- Night time -------
- Started with camera hexapods warmup and Calsys checkouts, but fiber spectrographs could not be enabled (OBS-1561). Due to this, white light flats could not be taken according to the required steps in the test case.
- Camera vacuum stabilization was confirmed by camera team at 02:34 UTC
- At 03:25 UTC, calibration attempts for BLOCK-T556 and BLOCK-T682 were stopped and switched to SuperBias (BLOCK-T382) test.
- Camera went to FAULT at 04:34 UTC (OBS-1597) and recovered at 05:00 UTC
- SuperBias frames completed at 08:40 UTC
- Dome and TMA parked afterwards.
- First 2 steps for minimal calibrations were skipped.

Daytime:
Once the camera pump cart was disconnected, fcs team run tests in the carrousel and the AutoChanger. We follow our procedure to test the impact of movements in the cryo vacuum pressure: rotator movements, filter changes, Azimuth and Elevation short slews at 5% velocity. Once we finished we moved to dynamic tests (5%, 10%, 20% velocity). We did not detect any impact in the cryo vacuum pressure (steady around 2.9e-8 Torr) and left the mount pointing at the calibration screen. (Trim heat capacity at around 91 W).
auxtel_summary:
---- Night time -----
Smooth night of observation, which started at 00:12 UTC and finished at 09:28 UTC


Daytime:
Checkouts were completed successfully. When starting to vent, the script faulted. This was because ATDome reported to be open 18% despite being closed. A restart of the Shutter-cRio solved the issue (see ticket with dome closing issues from last night OBS-1595).
Furthermore the ATBuilding Fan did not start when commanding it, cycling everything solved the issue (OBS-1596).

summary: We are back on-sky!  Smooth daytime preparations.  Two engineering tests plus a good chunk of FBS observations.  TMA was left pointed at the calibration screen as requested.
weather_summary: Clear and calm.  Humidity below 20% with low speed winds (<3 m/s).
simonyi_summary:
Nighttime

The optical alignment drifted quite far off by the end of the test, which will probably need to be repeated after some updates.  FBS observations got off to a rocky start with an AOS mis-configuration (OBS-1603) that cost 1 hour.  We did get 5 hours of uninterrupted FBS observations before executing the stray light BLOCK-T676, prior to the installation of the mid-level baffle.  The night ended with minimal daily calibrations, despite a minor fault with the LinearStage.104 (OBS-1604).

Daytime
Default TMA settings were switched back to 20% by Tiago R. Nominal checkouts went through without issues except for M2-Hex vibrations (OBS-1587).
auxtel_summary:

DIMM.2 worked all night after a remote kick from Lukas, but DIMM.1 remains unavailable.

summary: Critical loss of all 4 Glycol Chillers during the day which endangered the health of the Camera. Luckily the engineering team recovered the Chillers fast and the Camera team was able to avoid a warmup so that we could go onsky!
weather_summary: Clear skies. humidity <10% wind speed ~5m/s
simonyi_summary:
---- Night time-----

Unfortunately we lost the night due to a major camera firmware issue that caused an unexpected ~60 W increase in focal plane power after the glycol outage. The problem was traced to unintended activation of the REB jitter cleaner in the latest firmware update.
The temporary solution is to revert to a previous firmware version, but due to the time and associated risks, camera team decided that the recovery will be done in the morning.
We also got many alerts and faults with the OSS due to El lim+ Interlock (OBS-1511) and EIB software error (OBS-1495)
TMA Parked at zenith and mirror lowered.

---- Daytime ----

We had 2 big issues:

- All 4 Glycol Chillers switched off due to a loss of hvac.cp.lsst.org. The exact reason and mechanism will be discussed in FRACAS-344. As a short term solution, all chillers were turned back on in manual mode. During the time without glycol, all camera cooling switched off (PCS and Cryo) causing an extremely critical situation for the camera. After the camera was stabilized again by Stuart, all glycol chillers were returned to supervised mode. 
The camera was fully recovered at xyz.

- TMA ETPB which caused a GIS Faulting most systems, this happened while unparking from Horizon. We were able to clear all interlocks except a EL lim+ interlock signal. However, ETPB triggered again. David JM. remotely rebooted the TMA-IS which solved the issue (likely related to SUMMIT-12075).

Besides this, checkouts succeeded and M1M3 tests were performed by Petr.
We vented the dome at ... and went on sky at ...
auxtel_summary:
---- Night time-----
Smooth night of observation

---- Daytime ---
Work on ATSpectrograph and ATDome cRIOs in the morning. After this we had some issues with an ATMCS Estop which prevented ATMCS to Enable. Reason for this was an opening of the safety gate without a prior bypass and an activation of the safety gate escape release early in the morning. After this Estop signal was released, checkouts and venting went without issues.

summary:
Back on sky with the first FBS with Alerts!

Auxtel was running smoothly until 5:30 am. Then, ATAOS went to fault. We recovered it and shutdown the auxtel.

Simonyi FBS survey was smooth throughout the night with minor issues.
weather_summary: During the night, the average air temperature was ~17 °C. The average relative humidity was ~8%. The average wind speed was ~4 m/s.
simonyi_summary:
--- Nighttime ----
We started the night with the initial telescope alignment. We had to repeat it because dof's were set back to 0 after cycling MTAOS due to a misconfig (OBS1612).  We then began again the FBS LSST survey at 01:08 UTC and completed the first field (EDFS) in approximately 1.5 hours. After that, we started the pointing model block at 02:36 UTC and completed it at 04:14 UTC. During this run, we experienced a dome fault and lost about 20 minutes while recovering and restarting the pointing model block. The FBS survey then resumed. Scheduler got error at 6:37 UTC. The camera was not accepting ACTION/CONFIGURATION commands despite no clear fault condition (OBS1613). Yousuke restarted focal-plane subsystem which clear the error. Then, we resumed the scheduler. End of the night at 10:00 UTC leaving Minimal calibrations running.

---- Day time ----
Day was still in the shadow of last nights issues. Camera team was working on the firmware issues which prevented us to go on sky last night and the Daycrew worked on the TMA EStop/ElLim+ which failed TMA and Mirror twice yesterday.

Notable points:
- Camera team was able to fix the issue until 21 UTC, right before dinner.
- Louver B1 was faulting end of last night and during the Domehandover. It will not be used to night (see for details OBS-1609)
- Freddy M. discovered that the pressured oil inside the OSS Accumulators, which is supposed to smoothly/safely escort the TMA down in case of an fault, is actually releasing into the oil tank instead into the bearings. This issue might be there from the very beginning and increases the risk/wear on the bearings (details OBS-1607).
- David JM. gave OS an instruction how to recover the Estop/ElLim+ issue (He created also a empty ticket OBS-1608 which might be filled).

All checkouts performed without issues. Dome opened at 23:30 UTC.
auxtel_summary:
Nightime
Auxtel observation was smooth until 08:30 UTC. Then, ATAOS went to fault. We reboot the cRio and shutdown the Auxtel.

Daytime
Calm day for auxtel, checkouts and venting without issues.

summary: Rubin First Alerts FBS night - we were on-sky all night with just few minor issues.
weather_summary: Warm (16-19 degC) afternoon with low humidity (10–20%) and winds below 4 m/s. Evening temperature remained high - when opening the dome at Sun el. -6 the temperature outside was still 2C higher than inside. Some cloud cover increased toward sunset but the start of night remained clear, with low humidity and no wind. 05:00 UTC clouds started forming in the west and remained until morning.
simonyi_summary:
Nighttime------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We started the Active Alerts FBS at 00:34 UTC. After first 30 minutes the MTMount and MTPtg faulted with MTMount Azimuth axis fault (OBS-959), this faulted OSS and PS - all were recovered without issues and we resumed the scheduler with time loss ~45 minutes. 
While running the scheduler, the Residual AOS FWHM was >0.5, perhaps due to rapid elevation change, or slow thermalization due to high temp. in the evening. We stopped the scheduler to re-run the initial alignment, we had to run it three times to achieve Residuals <0.5 - time loss ~60 minutes. 
5:00 UTC clouds started to form in the West affecting the images, but overall only <1 mag extinction and zeropoints looking good so we continued with the First Alerts FBS. 
We had MTRotator and MTPtg fault, caused supposedly by some connection issue (OBS-749), both cycled back to enabled and resumed the scheduler without any delays.
We run the BLOCK-T676, did not detect any stray light in the images. 
Afterwards we returned back to T691 for final minutes. 
While running T664 Minimal Daily Cals LinearStage 104 Faulted so we skipped taking flats for tonight (OBS-1616). 

Daytime -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We started the day by cleaning the mirrors; the procedure was smooth. Afterward, the rubber mat was placed back over the camera.

Regarding M1M3, the bump and hardpoint activities were skipped today since they were performed yesterday.

All daily checkouts were completed without major issues. During the TMA unpark, an EIB Manager software error occurred, which was resolved by clearing the fault on the TMA EUI (see OBS-1615 for details).

During the operations handover, ESS: 108 started to fault (FRACAS-325). After some time and two additional faults, it was decided to keep it in standby.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
auxtel_summary:
Nighttime ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

After starting the scheduler we noticed the images were out of focus - we followed the obs-ops procedure and re-run the latiss wep align which fixed the issue and we resumed the scheduler. The rest of the night continued smoothly, until the end of night when the cloudy sky prevented latiss from finding centroid and  latiss_acquire_and_takesequence faulted multiple times. Anyways, we continued to collect data until Sun el. -12 when we stopped the scheduler and shutdown. 


Daytime ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Flawless performance for the daytime, mirrors cleaned today.

summary: Dew point higher than the operational limit throughout the entire night prevented us from opening the dome and observing with Simonyi, we lost the total 09:10 hours.
weather_summary: The day started windy (8 m/s) with 30–50% cloud cover. By sunset, the skies had cleared and winds had calmed to 3 m/s. During the night, the dew point was very high, rising to ~8C, along with the humidity which remained at 70 - 75%.
simonyi_summary:
Nighttime ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The dew point remained high, with difference to Dynalene <-4C almost entire night, preventing us from opening the dome. Upon visual inspection of the TMA we were seeing a lot of water condensation on all non-insulated Dynalene pipes so it was necessary to remain parked at horizon the whole night. The total observing time loss 09:10 hours.

04:17 AM the IPSec tunnel connection to USDF has gone down due to an ampath network outage. However, since we are only observing with Auxtel and there is no IT support currently at the summit, the issue will be addressed early in the morning (IHS-9676).

Daytime -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The day began with the daily calsys checkouts following faults encountered late the previous night. A low-level command was required to place the LED Projector in standby mode. 

The camera was also checked after an early-day fault; however, no troubleshooting was needed as the system self-recovered after one hour.

No further issues were observed afterward. The TMA could not be moved during the daytime due to the dew point and the associated risk of condensation.

The M1M3 bump and hardpoint tests were skipped today.
auxtel_summary:
Nighttime ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Beginning of the night while preparing to go on-sky we had a mount timeout and had to cycle the ATMCS to move the mount. This solved the issue (OBS-1617) and we continued to go on-sky and to observe without further issues. During the night we continued monitoring the dew point and humidity, however, for Auxtel it remained within operational limits. 


Daytime -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Flawless performance for the daytime.

summary: Another night off-sky. Even though the dew point decreased tonight, condensed water on the TMA and Dynalne pipes prevented us from unparking the telescope from horizon. Total time loss was the entire night, 09:10 hours. M1M3 Fault due to issues with Force Actuator 334.
weather_summary:
——— Nighttime  ——— 
The humidity had decreased slightly after the sunset and hovered around 50% throughout the night. Winds around 3 m/s at the beginning of the night dropped to 0. Dew point had decreased, since 4:00 the difference to dynalene temp. was above the operational limit, around ~ -1C. 

——— Dayttime  ——— 

Some clouds, humidity ranged from 65% to 36%.  Dynalene temperature and Inside/outside dew point difference were ~-3 deg.
simonyi_summary:
——— Nighttime  ——— 
Beginning of the night we were closed due to high dew point. Around 02:00 UTC the dewpoint started decreasing, finally reaching the condition for the dewpoint operational limit around 04:00. We started venting to dry the condensed water for about 2 hours until 6:00, however, when we went to L8 to check there was still a lot of water accumulated the Dynalene pipes and on the TMA. Hence, we remained parked at horizon without going on sky for the rest of the night. 

——— Daytime  ——— 

Condensation present on the TMA in the morning, afternoon inspections and walkaround. We were outside operational dewpoint limit during the day so TMA remained parked at horizon, we run nominal tests except for M1M3 tests. At 22:55 UTC M1M3 FAULTED, after recovery it faulted 3 times (OBS-1621). When going to L8 we heard a strange hissing sound around the TEA (OBS-1620). After 1 hour passed the M1M3 CSC was recovered by simply Enabling the CSC and continued running without issues. We performed actuator Bump test which passed without issues.
auxtel_summary:
——— Nighttime  ——— 
Smooth night, collecting data from and until sun elevation -12. 

——— Daytime  ——— 

Daily checkouts run ok, weekly calibrations required dome alignment and ATWhiteLight was not powering off (OBS-1619)

DIMM.1 will not be operational until an UPS is installed.
DIMM.2 had been troubleshooted and was working fine throughout the night.

summary: Rubin Alerts FBS night. LSSTCam focal-plane issue caused 0.6 hr time loss, MTAOS and MTRotator faulted multiple times without causing delays. Late night parking position was not specified in the plan so we finished at calibration screen, mirror covers retracted, OSS, PS on.
weather_summary: The afternoon was warm (16–20 °C), with variable dew point conditions that improved by the end of the afternoon, matching the requirements to move the TMA and proceed with observations. During the night, humidity remained around 50% and dew point continued to decrease, dew point to Dynalene difference reached >-2C, in the morning >0C. No wind and temperatures around 13C.
simonyi_summary:
Nighttime-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Started the initial alignment at Sun el. -12 and the First Alerts FBS at Sun el. -14 (00:27 UTC). The alerts broker was finally up streaming the alerts at ~02:20 UTC. The delay was due to an emergency outage of REUNA betwenn LS and Santiago, affecting the ISPec tunnel. 
While taking an image, we had LSSTCam focal-plane issue (OBS-1628), which required camera expert to resolve - time loss 00:36 hr. 
Other than that, we had four faults of MTAOS (a new time-out error; OBS-1629) and two faults of MTRotator (old error of delayed telemetry from CCW; OBS-922) which were troubleshooted immediately, did not cause delays.
We had a Fault of LinearStage:104 when trying to Enable it due to a connection issue (OBS-1616), however, on second try we were able to Enable it and run the Minimal Daily Cals without further issues.

In all we got at least ~8 hrs of on-sky time, factoring in the time-losses. 
Seq id to ignore--> 
169: trails due to MTPtg fault. 

Daytime --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The day started with routine tests, without issues. A small particle was found glued to the encoder tape (see OBS- 965 for details).

The main task during the day was to disable the M1M3 actuator 334. As part of this task, it was necessary to enter the cell to close the air valve. The work was completed in time to proceed with observations without any loss of observing time. Special thanks to Kevin F., B. Quint, and Michael R. for their support.
M1M3 hard point and bump tests was performed after M1M3 work.

The dome showed some alarms; please see OBS-1627 and OBS-1626 for details.
auxtel_summary:

On sky from and until Sun elevation -12.

AuxTel had error-free performance during the daytime; however, we noted that the venting fan was not working (see OBS-1622 for details).

summary: FBS on sky all night, and we accomplished more than 3000 filter changes since the start of Camera operations!

auxtel_summary:
---- Nightime----
Smooth night with zero faults/issues.  

——— Daytime  ——— 

During daily checkout we encountered an ATMCS–ATPtg communication issue (OBS-1633), temporarily resolved by Manuel G.

Fritz inspected the extractor fan (OBS-1622), determined hardware is working fine; it seems the CSC is unable to command it. We operated manually during venting.
