Auxtel on sky since 12:25AM UTC.

Smooth night with Auxtel.

summary: First Public alerts night! A fantastic night with sub-arcsec seeing. An almost-smooth night with sprinkles of CCW faults, Dome errors, and an MTAOS fault. We were on-sky for ~ 8.5 hrs (637 science visits)
weather_summary: Ambient temperature throughout was ~12C, with relative humidity coasting at 52% and winds dying out as we progressed into the night.
simonyi_summary:
——— Nighttime ———

* 00:06 UTC Initial alignment start (-10 deg Sun El)
* Initial alignment was successful on the third attempt--- First attempt was fraught with MTMount+MTPtg+MTRotator fault (CCW stopped following; OBS-738), second time one of the `close-loop script failed. 
* FBS started at 00:30 UTC (Sun El -15.5 deg) with DIQ of 0.88" in r-band (AOS res 0.39"). 
* Seq 371 (~00:33 UTC) is the First Public Alerts image 
* AT 7:00 UTC --- CCW timeout caused MTMount to fault. Simultaneously Dome started throwing errors repeatedly. OCS queue managed to get stuck while running a script. It cost us 30 min of on-sky time 
* 7:35 UTC we decided to stop AuxTel observation to make the AT Queue available to resolve frequent dome errors and continue FBS observations.   
* 09:26 UTC FBS Observations stopped at -14.1 Sun Elevation
* 09:31 UTC DOme shutters+louvers closed (-12.7 deg Sun El)

In general LOVE was super-slow towards later half of the night. RA was also lagging behind in image ingestion on RubinTV. 

——— Daytime ———
* Electronics ran a Dynalene flow rate test and increased pressure at L6 manifold (from ~4.5 Bar to 8 Bar) and camera flow rate (from ~5.22 GPM to ~7.6 GPM)
* The Mechanical team cleaned the azimuth encoder tape.
* The Camera team coordinated with IT cleaning fiber connections to address LSSTCAM-148.
* We completed nominal daily tests, but note we observed oscillations in the M2 Hexapod (reported in OBS-1587).
auxtel_summary:
——— Nighttime ———

Smooth operations until 7:35 UTC, when we stopped them. AuxTel shutdown was bumpy (ATMCS faults). But through state-cycling ATCS and running a quick checkout, the shutdown was successful.  

——— Daytime ———
* Brian B. restored the remote command for the extractor fan (OBS-1622).
* We completed daytime checkout and venting successfully.

summary: It was a rocky night for both telescopes, but we did get some observing done with Simonyi. We were interrupted by some dew point constraints, telemetry faults (dome and mount), and slow LOVE response time. The dome was a bit spicy at the beginning (OBS-1644), and then got a lot spicy at the end of the night, and wanted to stay open to see the sunrise. We worked with on site electrical support to convince her to close, and no telescopes were harmed in the meantime.
weather_summary: high humidity most part of the day >55%, low windspeed <5m/s, and Temperature around ~14°C. Dewpoint was mostly high >6°C, reaching a diff with predicted dynalene of -2°C, opening limit. We suffered a bit of weather loss at the start of the night, but observed in calm and stable conditions throughout.
simonyi_summary:
--- Nighttime ----
After a delayed start on sky due to dew point constraints and dome opening errors, we got on sky around 02:45 UT. During FBS observations, we encountered several instances of CCW telemetry failures in the mount that cost about 2 hours, and the dome failure in OBS-1644 which delayed us getting on sky by almost 2 hours as well. OBS-1644 will be updated with the failures encountered in the morning and transferred into a FRACAS ticket. 

--- Daytime ----

During the day, Cycle 43 was successfully deployed to the summit. In parallel, a second test of the glycol recirculation pump was completed without having evident impact in the glycol distributed systems.
In addition, M2 was kept in close-loop via EUI which was upgraded to LabVIEW 2024 Q3 (64-bit). Nominal Camera/Dome/TMA/M1M3 checkouts were successful.

CalSys checkout failed due to a connection issue with the LEDProjector CSC. The problem was traced to the LJM library requiring an IP address instead of a hostname. Currently the troubleshoot is in progress.
auxtel_summary:
--- Nightitme ----
AuxTel had a rough night, primarily due to changes stirred up by the upgrades on summit during the day. We did not have the expertise available to get the attention to these issues that was needed, so we closed 3 hours before twilight after encountering yet another barrier to getting data. Most of the night was lost due to error, detailed in the OBS tickets listed. 


--- Daytime ----
LATISS software was retarted at 19:30 UTC due to the cycle 43 performed in the morning. 
AuxTel checkouts passed but during venting we got some Dome faults (OBS-1643). The third attempt we tried it worked and AuxTel remained venting. We closed the dome at 11:05 UTC since we reached 70% humidity.

summary: Smooth night except for frequent MTAOS faults. Calibration skipped due to fiber spectrograph issues.
weather_summary: good weather: low wind (<3m/s), low humidity (20%~50%), temperature ~13 deg over the night
simonyi_summary:
Nighttime:
Night crew took over after dome opened. Initial alignment went smooth and FBS started 12:30AM UTC.

Faults:
  * MTAOS faulted 8 times (OBS-1629).
  * CCW faulted (OBS-1645). Manually pulled CCW.
  * MTDome went to error once (OBS-646).
  * Can't enable fiber spectrograph 101 and 102 for calibration. Skipped calibration. (OBS-1314)

Events:
  * Power glitch at 08:12UTC and 08:57UTC. Generators ran for a few minutes.
  * MTAircompressor 2 went off following the 2nd power glitch. We received alert and brought it back.



Daytime:
- Some lagging effects after yesterday cycle 46 on LinearStages and FiberSpectrograf (Eric C); Watcher (Wouter van R.)  The MTAOS version was also rolled back by Tiago R. 
- DREAM required manual intervention (Fritz M.) . The CSC required a restart via ArgoCD.
- Nominal daytime checkout worked without issues except for the dome shutter handover. It required the intervention of the electrical team (details in OBS-1644).
auxtel_summary:
Daytime:
- Venting script failed due an MTDome timeout (OBS-1643).

Nighttime:
latiss_wep_align doesn't converge but jumps back and forth between better and worse, likely due to being out of focus by too much. Tiago helped to fix it. Back on sky from 12:40AM UTC.

summary:
Started observations on-time and image quality reported good PSFs right at the start of the night. We ran the FBS survey the whole night, with additional louver tests sprinkled in periodically while Simonyi was observing.  

There were multiple issues during the night—mostly from MTDome and MTMount faults—causing around 1.34hrs of time loss. Regardless, the AOS closed-loop responded well to the faults, and we did not need to use observing time to run closed loop alignment scripts.
weather_summary:
---Nighttime---
Weather was clear during the night. Temperatures were between 12-13°C with very low wind speeds (1-4 m/s) and low humidity (30-40%).

--- Daytime ---
Close to the sunset we got clear skies and Temperature ~13C. Humidity slightly above 45°C, windspeed ~2 m/s.
simonyi_summary:
---- Nighttime ---
* Weather conditions were good enough to begin on-sky observations around -10 deg sun elevation.

Observing Plan During Night:

* BLOCK-T539: Initial telescope alignment (23:58 — 00:12 UTC).
    * Re-ran block twice (SAL Index: 101525 & 101529) due to a timeout error. Sun elevation was -9 deg when we started initial alignment.

* BLOCK-T691: Simonyi FBS LSST Survey (00:16 — 9:38 UTC).

summary:
LSSTCam cryo vacuum investigation and camera rotator pin troubleshooting delayed night observations by over 5 hours. Yet despite the long delay, we were able to observe with Simonyi after 2 days of downtime.

simonyi_summary:
——— Nighttime ——— 
* We were delayed significantly from starting on-sky observations due to priority of LSSTCam cry vacuum investigation. Since the TMA was left in an idle state for multiple days, we had to complete all daytime tasks priority to going on-sky. We officially began night operations around 4:17 UTC (~5hrs observing time loss).
    * While getting ready to go on-sky, the OSS was taking too long to enable, prompting us to restart Chiller #2 on level 1 (OBS-1818).
    * There were additional problems enabling the MTRotator CSC due to lower-level interlocks. We had to re-engage the rotator locking pin on the camera (see OBS-1819 for details; ~2.62hrs of the total time loss dedicated to troubleshooting this issue).

Observing Plan During Night:

* BLOCK-T539: Initial telescope alignment (4:17 — 4:23 UTC).
    * Initial alignment was done in r-band.
    * AOS residuals were <0.4” by then end of alignment. Image analysis reported sub arcsecond PSF FWHM values.
    * The M1M3TS glycol pump shut off on its own around 3:30 UTC, and it was not recovered until 4:30 UTC (OBS-1114).

* BLOCK-T698: FBS-driven closed loop stability w/ MTAOS (4:27 — 6:30 UTC).
    * This block was completed in i-band.
    * Image quality reported PSF FWHM measurements between 0.6—0.7” for many of the image sequences. 
    * While monitoring on RubinTV, there were seldom any images that displayed noticeably bad assymetry in their PSF shapes.
    * We have a new image quality record! See sequence number 214 (PSF FWHM 0.57”).
    * Follow-up analysis from AOS team showed that the new normalization weights were not applied on this test. This test must be re-run another night.

* BLOCK-T614: AOS Stability Verification - Open Loop FAM (6:43 — 8:43 UTC).
    * Test was done at az = 0 deg. 
    * Start of the block was delayed due to M1M3 EGW pump recovery (OBS-1554, 0.17hrs time loss).
    * We had to restart the test because it was initially done in i-band instead (seq. 216) of u-band (seq. 263).

* BLOCK-T720: AOS Alternating-Elevation Stability - Open Loop FAM (8:49 — 9:39 UTC).
    * We ran the test at az = 90 deg. The field might be a little too crowded, but we continued due to time constraint near the end of night.
    * We terminated a loaded block prematurely, so we had to re-enable the scheduler after starting the initial alignment ( ~ 0.17hrs time loss).
        * Observatory state reset while re-enabling, so we manually set it to OPERATIONAL at 9:05 UTC.

* BLOCK-T717: Quintuplets w/ FAM measures at two donut sizes (9:40 — UTC).
    * This block was unable to run on BTS, but we still attempted it tonight given we had ~30min left to observe.
    * We ran this block at az = 90 deg near the beginning of astronomical twilight, so it may be affected by the sun beginning to rise.
    * We stopped this test at 10:06 UTC because the sun was reaching -12deg of elevation and we were only halfway through the parameter_march_lsstcam.py script.
    * M1M3TS glycol pump unexpectedly turned off at 9:20 UTC, and was not noticed for ~40min (OBS-1114).

* Closed MTDome by 10:10 UTC (HVAC in daytime configuration) and took z-Band FLAT-OFFs (BLOCK-T636) at 10:15 UTC.
 


——— Daytime ——— 
It was a bumpy day, with observations starting later than planned. Most of the daytime was spent addressing a camera leak workaround, which will require additional follow-up work. As a result, preparations for on-sky operations were delayed.

The camera team continued monitoring the vacuum at the start of observations. The TMA was handed over to observers at 22:20 UTC, followed by the camera at 22:38 UTC.

The main issues encountered were:

A problem related to the deployable platforms (see OBS-1817), which required approximately one hour of troubleshooting.
The OSS failed to power on (see OBS-1818). About 30 minutes were spent attempting to start it before it ultimately failed, without generating any alerts.

These calibrations may need to be repeated.

* Priority of Simonyi movement demonstrations for guests at the summit delayed on-sky procedures to not start until around 00:15 UTC (~1 hr of time loss). Other than that we were on-sky with fewer issues compared to previous nights.
* M1M3TS glycol pump has been disabled for the night due to connection issues prohibiting us to recover it (OBS-1820). This will likely impact the AOS donuts with the presence of “dalmatian spots” in the donuts. 

Observing Plan During Night:
* BLOCK-T539: Initial telescope alignment (00:21 — 00:30 UTC).
    * Initial alignment was done in i-band.
    * AOS residuals were <0.4” by then end of alignment. Image analysis reported sub arcsecond PSF FWHM values.

* BLOCK-T698: FBS-driven closed loop stability w/ MTAOS (00:32 — 2:33 UTC).
    * We confirmed that the new normalization weights configurations (v3) were applied on this test.
    * This block was completed in i-band.
    * Image quality reported PSF FWHM measurements between 0.7—0.8” for many of the image sequences. 

* BLOCK-T720: AOS Alternating-Elevation Stability - Open Loop FAM (2:39 — 5:13 UTC).
    * We confirmed that MTAOS was reverted back to its original version (v2) before starting this test after BLOCK-T698.
    * First initial alignment attempts reported AOS residuals of ~0.5”. 
        * PSFs were also assymetric upon inspection in the rapid analysis in RubinTV.
    * As a test, we loaded the new MTAOS version again, and the residuals were 0.45” after initial alignment.
    * After running this comparison a few times, we decided to continue this test with the old MTAOS configuration (v2), but interesting results came from this test. More discussion can be found on the #commissioning-aos Slack channel.

* BLOCK-T717: Quintuplets w/ FAM measures at two donut sizes (5:17 — 6:53 UTC).
    * This block also used the old (v2) MTAOS configuration. 
    * We also re-ran the initial alignment procedure prior to starting the test.

* BLOCK-T624: Simonyi LSSTCam Feature Based Scheduler LSST Survey (7:12 —  UTC).
    * We set the MTAOS back to the new (v3) configuration.
    * We had to re-enable the scheduler, causing ~15min delay in observations.

    * BLOCK-T721 failed to run because we were unable to set-up CBP using setup_calsys_flats.py (sequence_name “setup_cbp” was not recognized, nor found in ts_observatory_control on GitHub).

* M1M3 went to fault twice. It faulted in the morning because of the issue in the thermal system and in the evening it went to fault because of the active interlock triggered by cell open door. (OBS-1822)

summary:

Simonyi TMA azimuth axis still awaiting alignment of one encoder head. LSSTCam cryo capacity is adequate (34 W at 22 deg elevation), and vacuum behavior remains under observation. A TEA Dynalene leak happened in the morning. Fortunately the Dynalene is from the heat exchanger and is not shared with the Camera. We kept the TMA at horizon for repair.

——— Nighttime ———
22:44 - 23:30 UTC initial alignment, interrupted by MTMount fault followed by failing to home Az axis.
23:30 UTC: FBS resumed.

* FBS continued all night with multiple interruptions of MTMount fault (OBS-1467) which improved after we switched the CCW Drive form 1 to 2. After the switch the Mount faulted only three times. 

* Multiple MTDome Errors cleared during the night (OBS-646) did not cause any delays.

* Issue with the right Workstation required restart of the machine (OBS-1898).

* At 08:40 we had an Error of the MTDome Shutter drives (OBS-1900).

* At 09:43 we had a Fault of the Scheduler (OBS-1899) which was due to an unknown cause and was self-fixed a while later.

* At the end of night, when we went up to L8 we noticed that the fans on the TMA are off, probably were off the whole night. 

* We completed the minimal daily cals and parked the telescope with mirror lowered, DP extended for mirror cleaning, OSS and PS off and M2 left in close loop for software upgrades.

* Power cut at the end of the night - issues with both Dynalene and Glycol, the glycol chiller 2 is off and setpoints are off as well. Compressor 2 was off as well and needed restart. Electrical support came to the summit to help restart Chiller 2, however the supervised mode was disabled so he was not able to. Camera remained out of danger zone. 

——— Daytime ———

Nominal daily tasks. M1M3 cell work during the day, serviced FA120, and they managed to recover FA 322. Bump test passed flawlessly today. 

There was a power outage during the dome handover (~19:55 UTC), all system recovered fine.

——— Nighttime ——— 
* Due to issues related to daytime troubleshooting (see Daytime section for details), we were delayed from on-sky operations until 00:38 UTC (~2hrs observational time loss).
* We observed tonight with all louvers opened and with the TMA/Dome fans powered on. 
* TMA performance settings were at 10% due to disabled M1M3 FA 428.

Observing Plan During Night:
* BLOCK-T539: Initial telescope alignment (00:43 — 00:52 UTC).
    * Initial alignment was done in i-band.
    * Camera hexapod compensation mode was disabled, despite CSC telemetry reporting it as enabled. We troubleshooted and redid the aligment at 00:48 UTC (OBS-1249).

* BLOCK-T624: Simonyi LSSTCam Feature Based Scheduler LSST Survey (00:58 - 9:46 UTC).
    * We had multiple instances of MTDome azimuth drives going to Error state (OBS-646).

Completed one AOS test, and then switched to the survey for the remaining time. We also captured ToO follow-up observations!
weather_summary:
——— Nighttime  ——— 
Cloudy sky overall, but we were able to observe through them for a majority of the night. Temperatures between 10-12°C with humidity 10-20% and windspeeds 5-10m/s.


——— Daytime  ——— 

Cloudy and warm day. Temperature ranged 11 -16  °C, mild to moderate winds < 8 m/s, and low humidity 5- 17 %
simonyi_summary:
——— Nighttime ———
*  Dome opened when Sun altitude was -4 deg (22:17 UTC)
*  We tried Initial alignment when Sun was at -10 deg but clouds prevent it, so we waited until 23:00 UTC to start.
*  Around 1:00 UTC we prioritized the AOS Alternating-Elevation Stability test (BLOCK-T720), which ran for only one hour. We selected 70 to 60deg for the priority angles.
*  LSST Survey started around 1:30 UTC and continued for the remainder of the night (10:44 UTC).
  *  ToO program started around 2:45 UTC! For those interested, see sequence numbers 189-195.
*  We closed dome at 10:44 UTC and started minimal daily calibrations at 10:56 UTC. We did not take biases or darks to prioritize turning off HV Bias at the end of the night.

——— Daytime ———
Day crew cleaned the mirrors after some open/close shutters tests, and camera team continued vacuum leak investigation.

OSs nominal checkouts, except for the mirror tests due to time constraints.
auxtel_summary:
——— Nighttime ———
AuxTel was ready to go on sky but clouds didn’t allow to continue. Dome closed at 23:13 UTC, but was reopened around 00:30 UTC. There was a single incident in which the survey pointed AuxTel below normal operational limits (OBS-2012). Shutdown was at 10:44 UTC.


——— Daytime ———

Day crew cleaned the mirror in the afternoon. 

Checkouts passed. During venting we noticed the extractor fan was not running, Fritz troubleshoot until it finally worked, see details in (OBS-1654).

summary:
We start focused on CBP filter sweeps for the night due the clouds. 

Clouds cleared up around 5:30 UTC, so we were able run the survey for around 4-5 hours. ToO follow-up observations were taken around 6:15 UTC due to on-sky delay.
weather_summary:
——— Nighttime  ——— 
Weather was very cloudy for most of the night. Temperatures between 9-11°C with humidity 30-50%. Wind speeds were around 0-5m/s.

By 5:30 UTC the clouds started to clear. However, seeing and PSF measurements reported between 1.5-2.0 arcsec while observing.

——— Daytime  ——— 

Cloudy and warm day. Temperature ranged 10 - 15  °C, mild to moderate winds < 7 m/s, and low humidity 5-21 %
simonyi_summary:
——— Nighttime ———
*  Dome opened when Sun altitude was -2 deg (22:04: UTC)
*  Initial alignment when Sun was at -10 deg (22:39UTC) but had to stopped at 23:33UTC due to clouds faulting MTAOS.
*  By 02:00 UTC, we decided to switch to in dome testing, as the clouds were not clearing by the time ToO observations were expected to occur. 
*  When closing the dome for calibration tests, we notice an issue with the park_dome script that did not properly park the dome in its normal position (OBS-2014).
*  At 3:00 UTC we started the CBP Filter Sweep (BLOCK-T339) in the IR wavelengths at two pointings. We had to re-enable the tunable laser CSC multiple times prior to starting (OBS-1823).
*  Clouds cleared up around 5:20 UTC, so after completing half of the calibrations, we switched back to on-sky operations.
*  Dome azimuth drives kept going to error state, stopping us from unparking (OBS-646).
*  Rapid analysis was very slow on RubinTV. We had an instance where the MTAOS faulted due to RA output errors (OBS-1532). See thread on #summit-announce for futher discussion.
*  We started initial alignment again at 6:00 UTC and started the survey at 6:10 UTC. ToO observations were taken at the start of the survey, around 6:15 UTC (seq 268-272).
* Closed dome at 10:45 UTC and started minimal daily calibrations were attempted at 11:00 UTC. Fibserspectrograph 102 failed to enabled (OBS-1216), so we shutdown after two attempts.

——— Daytime ———
Open/close shutters tests repeated, work done in M1M3 cell and mirror upper deck, and laser tracker tests.

Observers run nominal checkouts, including the mirror tests. Twice the M1M3 thermal scanners windows machines rebooted without M1M3CSC going to FAULT nor STANDBY (OBS-2013).

We encountered an issue with parking the dome script (OBS-2014).
L8 fans are not working (OBS-2009).

At around 23:29 UTC chiller #4 went off, issue described by OBS-2015, recovered by ~00:10 UTC
auxtel_summary:
——— Nighttime ———
Auxtel started observations at 22:36 UTC, we closed due to clouds at 23:30 UTC. Around 5:30 UTC AuxTel was back to observing (~6hrs lost due to weather). Shutdown was at 10:45 UTC.


——— Daytime ———

Checkouts passed. 
Venting run without issues (extractor fan worked ok).

summary: Nearly flawless night observing with Simonyi and AuxTel. Partially completed a single AOS engineering test, and ran the survey for the majority of the night. We shutdown 1hr early due to one of the observers not feeling well.
weather_summary:
%%%%%%%%%%%%  Night %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
Pretty calm and stable night. Temp ~ 12-13 C, Wind ~ 0-5 m/s, Humidity 13-14%. Sky was clear. 


%%%%%%%%%%%% Daytime %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

Warm afternoon; venting began with the Sun at -3° while outside temperatures remained relatively high. Moderate winds (~4 m/s, Pointing 4) and stable humidity (~19%).
simonyi_summary:
%%%%%%%%%%%%  Night %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

- The enclosure was opened for venting with the Sun at an elevation of -3°. We experienced a warm afternoon.
- Initial alignment began with the Sun at an elevation of -12 degrees.
- 23:05 - 23:58 UTC BLOCK-T720 (1.0) AOS Alternating-Elevation Stability, done to 70 - 50, 70 -30 was interrupted due to IQ.
- 00:10 - 9:45 UTC BLOCK-T624 (2.0) Simonyi LSSTCam Feature Based Scheduler LSST Survey
  - We stopped the survey 1hr early because an observer was not feeling well.
- Closed dome at 10:00 UTC and ran minimal daily calibrations at 10:08 UTC.

Issues: 
- We lost MT Aircompressor 2 between 04:25 to 04:30 UTC. Simply recovered remotely.
- MTRotator low level controller fault at 08:30 UTC (OBS-1481). 
- During the night, there were delay on RubinTV cluster several times. It was even worse in the crowded field.


%%%%%%%%%%%% Daytime %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

We had a late start due to fumigation activities, with daytime checks beginning at approximately 11:30 local time. Overall, it was a smooth day with only issue related to the fiberspectograph (OBS-1949), that was recovered with help of E. Dennihy and E. Coughlin
The OS team could not perform this troubleshooting due to credential restrictions. A ticket requesting the necessary access has been created (OBS-2016).

The majority of the available time was dedicated to camera vacuum leak hunting, performed by Y. Utsumi. Due to the limited daytime window, only the mandatory checks were completed. We also hosted a group of visitors at the summit during the day.

No M1M3 tests were performed today.
No calibrations were carried out during this daytime period.
auxtel_summary:
%%%%%%%%%%%%  Night %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

Flawless performance, again. On-sky observation was finished at 9:45 UTC. We shutdown AuxTel 1hr early because an observer was not feeling well. 

%%%%%%%%%%%% Daytime %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

Flawless performance, no calibrations taken today

summary:
Relatively smooth except for a glycol chiller 2 failure after power glitch, and Auxtel CSC faults.
Closed early at 4am due to backup shift drove to reach the summit.
weather_summary:
——— Nighttime  ——— 
Air temp 13~14 deg, RH 17%, wind < 2m/s.

——— Daytime  ——— 

Cirrus and warmer day. Temperature ranged 15-19°C, low winds < 5 m/s, and low humidity 11-16 %.
simonyi_summary:
——— Nighttime ———
22:23 UTC: Dome opened (Sun elevation -5.8 degrees).

22:51 UTC - Initial alignment started when Sun was at -11 deg. 

We did not run BLOCK-T720 at the start of the night because DIMM seeing was variable and there were clouds passing by.

23:06 UTC we started the Feature Based Scheduler.

The night crew took over while telescope on sky with FBS running. FBS ran the whole night till the early shutdown at 4AM local. We queued up a set_summery_state to put MTCam in OFFLINE after the daily darks, in preparation for dome work in the day.

Issues:
  -- power glitch at 06:30 UTC, and glycol chiller 2 stopped (OBS-1214). Oscar remotely started it.

——— Daytime ———
We started the day with alarms from the HVAC system and Chiller 2. With the support of the on-call experts, the issue was identified and the systems were successfully recovered.

We performed the TMA walk around and then run the CBP BSS investigation test (BLOCK-T747) Yousuke lead us and Elana support us remotely, details reported in OLE and in the test execution.

After lunch Yousuke continue camera leak investigation, while observers continue daily checkouts, but we had to skip the M1M3 tests and Camera hexapod warmup.

During the TMA uparking, MTMount faulted due to elevation sync controller issue (OBS-2017) and then the mirror covers failed to open (OBS-2018).
auxtel_summary:
——— Nighttime ———

Auxtel started observations at 22:34 UTC. Auxtel closed at 4AM local.

Issues:
  -- A few CSC including ATMCS went to fault (not connected; OBS-1858). ATMCS faulted again after enabling. Restarting ATMCS cRio solved the issue.

——— Daytime ———

Checkouts passed.

Calibrations taken, note the dome has noticeable light inside.

Venting script failed (vent gate did not open and then the extractor fan did not turn on (OBS-1654), we vent without the extractor fan.

summary: Both Simonyi and Auxtel observed throughout the night without any issue. End of the night around 11:00 UTC.
weather_summary:
Daytime temperature 15-18 deg C.  Relative humidity ~13%.  Wind speed < 5 m/s.

Seeing was ~0.6" at the start of the night.

Night time average air temperature ~9 feg C, average relative humidity ~ 22%, and average wind speed ~ 9 m/s.
simonyi_summary: The daytime checkouts were nominal.  We skipped the M1M3 hard point and bump tests.  Before the dome handover, Lorenzo performed a locking pin movement test.  The dome shutter and louvers were opened at 22:10 UTC, and we began the initial alignment at 22:54 UTC.  At 23:05 UTC, we began BLOCK-T720 AOS Alternating-Elevation Stability - Open Loop Full Array Mode.  At 00:31 UTC, we started BLOCK-T668 Closed Loop TARTS which completed around 2:20 UTC. After this, FBS survey was run throughout the night  without any interruption. We performed minimum daily calibration at the end of the night.
auxtel_summary:
The daytime checkouts were normal.  The only exception was the faulting of ATMCS and ATPtg during venting due to the nasmyth 2 velocity error being exceeded (OBS-2019).  The components were re-enabled, and venting continued without issue.

AuxTel began on-sky observations at 22:49 UTC.

Observed throughout the night without any issue. W shutdown auxtel around 10: 52 UTC.

summary:
Calibration night with many tunable laser faults.

Auxtel warming up over the night, in preparation for incoming storm. Turbo pump connected and running.
weather_summary:
The day was cloudy and windy, with winds around 10 m/s and low humidity ranging from 19% to 25%.

At the beginning of the night, thin clouds were passing through. Around 11:35 UTC, the weather conditions deteriorated, prompting us to suspend on-sky activities and begin the in-dome calibrations.

Night time:
temperature ~7 deg, wind ~ 12m/s, RH 26.2%. Cloudy whole night.
simonyi_summary:
Daytime %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

We completed the daytime checkouts nominally. The day crew requested that M1M3 be lowered to support work on the mirror coating chamber. Additional work was performed inside the cell to verify power to the PC's thermal scanner. Afterward, the M1M3 bump and hardpoint tests were completed successfully, and the mirror was raised. All tests passed.

Later in the day, a TMA PXI issue occurred during day crew activities.

Nighttime %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

We attempted to run the initial alignment (thin clouds passing), but after one attempt and a short waiting period, we decided to proceed with the in-dome calibrations as the weather conditions deteriorated.

11:30 UTC BLOCK-T750 (1.0) LSSTCam V BSS gain test with LED Flats.

Night crew took over at the end of T750. 

Blocks: 
  -- BLOCK-T339: 01:56 to 06:20 UTC. We ran step 4, step 12, and step 4 again. Seq 283-294 might be duplicated (marked in exposure log).
  -- BLOCK-T732: 07:35 to 09:J28UTC.  starting from step 9. We only had time to finish step 9 with g band filter scan, and we had to give up due to many tunable laser faults.

Issues:
  -- electrometer 102 keeps faulting. Elana helped to power cycle it.
  -- countless tunable laser faults which required PDU power cycle.
  -- daily calsys flats configuration failed (OBS-2022)
auxtel_summary:
There were minimal issues during the daytime activities. The Prepare for Vent script failed due to a timeout in the ATBuilding component (OBS-1654).

Auxtel stay closed. We went to Auxtel dome to connect the turbo pump and warming up latiss under Craig's instruction. Day crew will need to disconnect the turbo pump.

summary: Daytime activities were focused on preparing the observatory for the incoming winter storm.  There will be no further summit activities until at least Monday.
weather_summary: The winter storm is definitely approaching!  Wind speed > 15 m/s during the day.  Temperature 5-6 deg C. Clouds accumulated, mostly high altitude and there is some snowing on the far away mountains.
simonyi_summary: During the morning, Kevin and Danica connected the pump cart to warm up LSSTCam.  M2 and LSSTCam were covered with an anti-static tarp.  ComCam was also covered.  TMA is parked at horizon and az = 148 deg.  M1M3 is lowered.
auxtel_summary: The turbo pump was left connected.  The valve was closed and the turbo pump was powered down.  AuxTel was covered with a tarp.  Mario unexpectedly found vent gate #3 open.  He was unable to manually close it, so Fritz remotely assisted (OBS-2023).

summary: No summit staff or activities due to winter storm.  Summit conditions will be assessed no earlier than Monday.  Periodic remote monitoring will continue until then.
weather_summary: Winter weather - over night, temperatures dropped close to 0, no snow fall yet. During the day humidity rising to 60%.
simonyi_summary:
Status remains the same.  TMA remains parked at horizon and az = 148 deg with M1M3 lowered.  M2 and LSSTCamera remain covered.  Relevant updates regarding LSSTCamera can be found on the Rubin Observatory Slack channel #cam-operator.
4.4 magnitude earthquake E of Tongoy at 10:38:30 UTC, M1M3 HP forces within limits.  In the early afternoon, we turned ON all four TMA Top End Chiller cabinets because they were in fault.
auxtel_summary: Status remains the same.  AuxTel remains covered. The turbo pump remains connected but powered down and with the valve closed.

After sunset, the temperature started decreasing and seeing on the cameras it started snowing a lot.
simonyi_summary:
Another day and night of the snow storm. 
During a day there was a scheduled warm-up routine for generators Caterpillar (ESS:306), Mitsubishi (ESS:305), and Villa Rubin Generator.
Some water staines had been spotted on the TMA and below it. 
At 20:21:40 we had a short ~30s power cut which caused turning off of the dome lights (OBS-2024). The lights were turned back on by the electrical team. Another short power cut happened at 22:28 UTC.
auxtel_summary: AuxTel closed.

summary: Snow storm continues.
weather_summary:
Temperature stable just something below zero. Humidity high 99.9%. 
High winds > 20 m/s, we lost the wind speed sensor at 13:17 UTC.
Significant snow cover is now formed outside.
simonyi_summary:
Louver A1 is covered with snow and we can see snow gushing in around that area. There is some snow accumulated on L7 but nothing near the TMA. 
Multiple remote tests of the generators during the day and night which were all successful. 
M1M3 glycol flow dropped and the M1M3TS cRIO was restarted. Flow to M1M3 remains irregular due to TMA parked at horizon.
auxtel_summary: High humidity alarms in Auxtel.

summary:
The impact of the snowstorm has been severe: 
Due to storm damage to the power poles within the observatory property, a site-wide power outage and communication blackout have occurred; damage assessment and repairs will commence once the access road is cleared.

We fully lost the commercial power at 16:30 UTC and never came back. Due to this, we lost several components of the observatory, but all were recovered. After UPS was depleted at 23:31 UTC, the observatory began relying solely on the generator. The remaining fuel supply for the generators is projected to sustain operations for up to 8 days.
weather_summary: Full of clouds during the day. Temp ~ -2 C degree, wind ~ 15 m/s and 100% humidity.
simonyi_summary:
----- Daytime -----
- At 16:30 UTC (12:30 CLT), there was a power outage, and after this, the summit lost the commercial power. 
- ESS:404 and ESS:405 went to FAULT when the power outage happened at 12:30 CLT (16:30 UTC) - recovered. 
- Chiller:2 also went off from the power outage at 16:30 UTC (12:30 CLT) and was back in operation at 16:52 UTC (12:52 CLT).
- Kevin Reil reported at 17:13 UTC (13:13 CLT) that a storm-induced power pole failure had cut off commercial power and communications to the mountain, with site access required before damage assessment and repairs could begin.
- At 20:52 UTC (16:52 CLT), MTAircompressor:2 went off. Recovered in 5 mins.
- At 23:31 UTC (19:31 CLT), the UPS supporting the Telconor backup link has been fully depleted. Connectivity to the summit began to rely fully on the direct fiber link.
auxtel_summary: Continuous alarms in Auxtel due to high humidity.
